Title: New president of the Central Bank assumed office.
Subtitle: Con la presencia del Presidente de la Repblica del Paraguay, Don Horacio Cartes, se realiz el acto protocolar de asuncin del nuevo presidente del Banco Central del Paraguay (BCP), Don Carlos...
text: Mr. President of the Republic, Horacio Cartes Jara, Mr. Vice-President of the Republic, Juan Eudes Afara, Dear Ministers of the Executive Power, Members present, Ambassadors and Representatives of friendly countries, Representatives of International Organizations, Civil and Military Authorities present, Representatives of the Financial System, Colleagues of the Central Bank of Paraguay, Ladies and gentlemen First of all, I would like to thank the President of the Republic for the trust placed in me to lead the Central Bank of Paraguay, an institution recognized for the valuable and professional work it has been doing in recent years. It is a privilege and an honor to have the opportunity to collaborate again with our beloved country. Ladies and gentlemen A professor at my university frequently recalled that "those who do not learn from past mistakes run the serious risk of repeating them." In September 2008, with the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers, what would be the greatest economic and financial crisis of the last eighty years began. Every crisis is always painful, with pernicious economic and social consequences, but the so-called Great Recession has been particularly costly because of two factors. In the first place, and considering different measures, the economic collapse observed has only been surpassed by the Great Depression of the 30s of the last century. Second, the degree of synchronization of the economic slowdown was the greatest since that great global crisis of the early twentieth century. Despite the intensity of the shock and its synchronized spread, the impact of the 2008 global crisis was not homogeneous across countries. Among emerging economies, countries in Latin America were less affected than those in Eastern Europe: in our region, the economic contraction has been smaller and the recovery much faster. On the other hand, while all economies in this part of the world were affected by the crisis, the magnitude of the impact varied greatly across countries. Why did Eastern European economies perform worse economically than those in Latin America? Why the heterogeneity even between countries located in the same region? Was it the emerging economies innocent victims of imbalances originating in the financial sector of advanced countries? Or have there previously been weak economic policy frameworks that helped weaken some countries' resilience to external shocks? From 2010 onwards, global conditions changed substantially for the so-called emerging countries. Latin American economies, including Paraguay, have since benefited from a "double tailwind": high commodity prices (a result of the strong growth of the Chinese economy) and access to cheap international financing (a consequence of the counter-cyclical monetary policies implemented by advanced countries). This environment became a strong catalyst for the region's economies to grow very quickly. It would be at least unwise to expect these favorable external conditions to last forever. Both commodity prices and external financing conditions will need to normalize at some point. The winds are changing for our region. With terms of trade falling and the cost of external financing rising, countries' economic growth is likely to be less dynamic than over the past decade. In these circumstances, what should the authorities of our countries do to face less favorable external conditions without major setbacks? What are the main challenges of Policy in a new world where international financial conditions become more restrictive while the prices of the main products we export are reduced? Ladies and gentlemen The global crisis of 2008 has left valuable lessons for economists. This crisis had a double impact on the economies of our region that was adverse, exceptionally strong and sudden. During the global turbulence there was a collapse in commodity prices and, at the same time, a reversal of capital flows and a tightening of financing conditions. Therefore, keeping the differences in magnitude and speed, the 2008 crisis represented a confluence of negative shocks similar to those that will affect our countries in the near future given the normalization of monetary policy in the United States. That is why some lessons left by the recent global economic crisis (i.e. the answers to the first set of questions presented above) will be useful in limiting the negative effects of the new external shock. There is an extensive literature analyzing the differentiated impact that the last global crisis has had on countries. These studies find that Latin America has fared relatively better, not only compared to other regions but also compared to past crises. Positive exogenous factors (such as the rapid recovery of the Chinese economy) partly explain this improved performance. However, the main lesson of the recent crisis is that, beyond the importance of exogenous factors, good macroeconomic management during the boom years paid off. After the crises of the late nineties and early 2000s, Latin American countries strengthened their macroeconomic policy frameworks. They thus generated containment mechanisms, which allowed the execution of anti-cyclical policies after the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers. Currently, the policy framework chosen by most countries is based on prudent and rules-based macroeconomic policies; sound financial systems and capital markets; and integration into global goods and capital markets. This contributes to reducing the vulnerabilities of Latin American economies (including Paraguay) to possible external shocks. It must be recognized that there are certain aspects that can still be improved. For example, some countries would benefit from gradual fiscal consolidation. This would allow for the accumulation of resources that may be needed to deal with a slowdown in the future and help preserve fiscal credibility. Ladies and gentlemen The key challenge for our countries is therefore to take advantage of the current conditions still favourable to consolidate the progress made over the past decade and lay the foundations for growth. sustained under more adverse external conditions in the future. For the central bank, this means continuing to implement policies that are robust, agile and focused on clear objectives. Thus, in the new situation, monetary policy should be the first line of defence against a materialisation of risks. However, this will only be possible if the monetary policy framework is credible and inflation expectations are well anchored. The stability of the purchasing power of our currency, ready to celebrate 70 years since its creation, has been a conquest of society. Maintaining its value is a permanent challenge, the responsibility for which lies primarily with the central bank. The economic and social costs of high inflation, which has particularly harmful effects on a country's poorest population, are well known. I firmly believe that sustainable growth, which really brings benefits to all social strata, can only be achieved with low, stable and predictable inflation. Only in a scenario like this, the planning horizon of individuals and companies is extended and, consequently, the investments that generate employment, production and income are concretized. The fight against inflation has been, is and will be the best contribution of our central bank to promote sustained economic growth with greater social equity. To achieve this objective, we will continue to refine the inflation-targeting monetary policy scheme. The Central Bank of Paraguay has adopted since 2011, with encouraging results, this mechanism for the management of its monetary policy. This has resulted in lower and less volatile inflation rates. In addition, we will continue with a flexible exchange rate regime, the most coherent for an inflation-targeting framework. In the new situation, it will be essential for the central bank to continue to maintain exchange rate flexibility, which is a proven buffer against external shocks. At the same time, the monetary authority will have the option of intervening in the foreign exchange market in circumstances of uncertainty or high exchange rate volatility, as this may have harmful effects on the economy. Finally, it must be recognized that low and stable inflation does not guarantee financial stability, as the recent experience of a number of advanced economies demonstrates. Therefore, resilient and efficient financial systems are essential to avoid abrupt fluctuations in economic activity and prices. A financial system with these characteristics will be essential to successfully face eventual headwinds. In Paraguay, the successive financial crises of the nineties left immense costs for the treasury and society, postponing for many years the takeoff of our economy. Given the new situation, the central bank will need to continue to ensure the quality and efficiency of prudential regulation and supervision of financial institutions. The regulation and supervision of financial institutions have made great strides in recent years, in particular with the adoption of a more risk-based approach. Despite this, in terms of compliance with the Basel Core Principles for Oversight Effective banking, our regulatory framework is still below the average for the region. There are currently legal restrictions or impediments that make further progress in designing a regulation more in line with international standards. That is why, in order to achieve greater progress, changes to the existing legal framework will be required, modifications that will be made in consultation with affected parties. Improving prudential regulation and supervision of the financial system is a continuous and never-ending process. In this regard, the central bank will continue to improve its institutional and legal apparatus for monitoring the national financial system, with emphasis on ensuring financial stability. The regulation of banking and financial activities should also promote an inclusive financial system. This has two important implications. The first (or micro) is social, since financial inclusion contributes to the reduction of social inequalities and the economic development of any country. The second (or macro) is associated with the fact that financial inclusion strengthens the main transmission channel of monetary policy, which is exactly the financial system. Despite recent progress, our country still lags far behind the international average in terms of financial inclusion. Consequently, the central bank will implement a broad agenda to foster inclusion and financial education of the population. Ladies and gentlemen The Central Bank of Paraguay is, indisputably, an institution of excellence, recognized and respected in the country. I have no doubt that this recognition is due first and foremost to its employees, highly qualified professionals committed to the legal and institutional missions of the bank. Our human resources policy will continue to be based on the two factors that have enabled our success: the incorporation of career civil servants through competitive examinations and a strong staff training policy. I personally feel great satisfaction to be able to return to work after 10 years with my colleagues and friends at the central bank. My previous time at the institution helped me a lot to appreciate and value the capacity of the officials. Comrades, you are the best asset that BCP has, I count on all of you for success in this new management. At this point in my professional career, I would like to remember some very special people. To my father, who although he has left us physically when he was little, was always an inspiring source for me. To my mother, model of the beauty of the Paraguayan woman, who with her example of life has shown me the way forward and for whom there were never obstacles in life that are impossible to overcome. To my two children, an inexhaustible source of energy on weekdays until eleven at night and on weekends from seven in the morning, they are the joy of our home. To my wife, my partner, my friend, who unselfishly accompanies me through the journeys determined by my professional life. She is the pillar of our home, without her I would be nobody professionally and much less personally. To all of them my eternal gratitude for all that they have always given me and I love them very much from the bottom of my heart. Ladies and gentlemen With the recovery of the American economy, the extraordinary years of ease of financing and guaranteed growth that our countries have experienced during the last decade are gradually ending. The great challenge now is to prepare our economies to successfully face a more adverse external scenario. This is no time for complacency, but neither is this time for exaggerated pessimism. There are enviable macroeconomic conditions in Paraguay. In our country, the situation of banks is firm, the monetary policy framework is credible, the level of coverage of international reserves is adequate and public finances are solid. We have all the tools to continue guiding Paraguay along a path of sustained growth, full employment and progress and well-being for the entire population. Let's get to work. Thanks a lot. Asuncion, October 3, 2013
text_original: DISCURSO POSESI<ee>N DE CARGO PRESIDENTE BANCO CENTRAL DEL PARAGUAY CARLOS GUSTAVO FERN<e7>NDEZ VALDOVINOS Se<96>or Presidente de la Rep<9c>blica, Horacio Cartes Jara, Se<96>or Vice-Presidente de la Rep<9c>blica, Juan Eudes Afara, Se<96>ores Ministros del Poder Ejecutivo, Se<96>ores Parlamentarios presentes, Se<96>ores Embajadores y Representantes de pa<92>ses amigos, Se<96>ores Representantes de Organismos Internacionales, Autoridades Civiles y Militares presentes, Se<96>ores Representantes del Sistema Financiero, Compa<96>eros del Banco Central del Paraguay, Se<96>oras y Se<96>ores, En primer lugar, me gustar<92>a agradecer al Se<96>or Presidente de la Rep<9c>blica por la confianza depositada en mi persona para liderar el Banco Central del Paraguay, instituci<97>n reconocida por el valioso y profesional trabajo que ha venido realizando en los <9c>ltimos a<96>os. Es un privilegio y un honor tener la oportunidad de colaborar nuevamente con nuestro querido pa<92>s. Se<96>oras y se<96>ores Un profesor de mi universidad recordaba frecuentemente que <d2>quien no aprende de los errores pasados, corre el serio riesgo de volver a repetirlos<d3>. En setiembre de 2008, con la quiebra de Lehman Brothers, se iniciaba la que ser<92>a la mayor crisis econ<97>mica y financiera de los <9c>ltimos ochenta a<96>os. Toda crisis es siempre dolorosa, con perniciosas consecuencias econ<97>micas y sociales, pero la denominada Gran Recesi<97>n ha sido particularmente costosa por dos factores. En primer lugar, y considerando diferentes medidas, el colapso econ<97>mico observado solo ha sido superado por la Gran Depresi<97>n de los a<96>os 30 del siglo pasado. En segundo lugar, el grado de sincronizaci<97>n de la desaceleraci<97>n econ<97>mica fue el mayor desde esa gran crisis mundial de inicios del siglo veinte. A pesar de la intensidad del choque y de su propagaci<97>n sincronizada, el impacto de la crisis global del 2008 no fue homog<8e>neo a trav<8e>s de los pa<92>ses. Entre las econom<92>as emergentes, pa<92>ses en Am<8e>rica Latina fueron menos afectados que aquellos en Europa del Este: en nuestra regi<97>n, la contracci<97>n econ<97>mica ha sido menor y la recuperaci<97>n mucho m<87>s r<87>pida. Por otro lado, si bien todas las econom<92>as en esta parte del mundo fueron afectadas por la crisis, la magnitud del impacto vari<97> enormemente a trav<8e>s de los pa<92>ses. <c0>Porqu<8e> econom<92>as del este europeo tuvieron un peor desempe<96>o econ<97>mico que aquellas en Am<8e>rica Latina? <c0>Porque la heterogeneidad a<9c>n entre pa<92>ses localizados en una misma regi<97>n? <c0>Fueron las econom<92>as emergentes v<92>ctimas inocentes de desequilibrios originados en el sector de financiero de los pa<92>ses avanzados? <c0>O existieron previamente marcos de pol<92>tica econ<97>mica poco robustos que contribuyeron a debilitar la capacidad de resistencia de algunos pa<92>ses a choques externos? A partir del 2010, las condiciones globales cambiaron sustancialmente para los llamados pa<92>ses emergentes. Las econom<92>as latinoamericanas, incluyendo el Paraguay, se beneficiaron desde entonces por un <d2>doble viento a favor<d3>: altos precios de materias primas (resultado del fuerte crecimiento de la econom<92>a china) y acceso a financiamiento internacional barato (una consecuencia de las pol<92>ticas monetarias anti-c<92>clicas implementadas por los pa<92>ses avanzados). Este ambiente se convirti<97> en un fuerte catalizador para que las econom<92>as de la regi<97>n crezcan muy r<87>pidamente. Ser<92>a cuanto menos imprudente esperar que estas condiciones externas favorables perduren para siempre. Tanto el precio de las materias primas como las condiciones externas de financiamiento deber<87>n normalizarse en alg<9c>n momento. Los vientos van cambiando para nuestra regi<97>n. Con t<8e>rminos de intercambio a la baja y con el costo de financiamiento externo al alza, muy probablemente el crecimiento econ<97>mico de los pa<92>ses ser<87> menos din<87>mico que durante el decenio pasado. En estas circunstancias, <c0>qu<8e> deber<92>an hacer las autoridades de nuestros pa<92>ses para enfrentar sin mayores contratiempos condiciones externas menos favorables? <c0>Cu<87>les son los principales desaf<92>os de pol<92>tica en un mundo nuevo donde las condiciones financieras internacionales se vuelven m<87>s restrictivas mientras que los precios de los principales productos que exportamos se reducen? Se<96>oras y se<96>ores La crisis global del 2008 ha dejado valiosas lecciones para los economistas. Esta crisis tuvo sobre las econom<92>as de nuestra regi<97>n un doble impacto que fue adverso, excepcionalmente fuerte y s<9c>bito. Durante la turbulencia mundial existi<97> un desplome en los precios de las materias primas y, al mismo tiempo, una reversi<97>n de los flujos de capitales y un endurecimiento de las condiciones de financiamiento. Por lo tanto, guardando las diferencias en cuanto a magnitud y velocidad, la crisis del 2008 represent<97> una confluencia de shocks negativos similares a los que afectar<87>n a nuestros pa<92>ses en un futuro pr<97>ximo dada la normalizaci<97>n de la pol<92>tica monetaria en los Estados Unidos. Es por ello que algunas ense<96>anzas dejadas por la reciente crisis econ<97>mica mundial (es decir, las respuestas al primer conjunto de preguntas presentadas anteriormente) ser<87>n <9c>tiles para limitar los efectos negativos del nuevo shock externo. Existe una extensa literatura analizando el impacto diferenciado que ha tenido la <9c>ltima crisis global en los pa<92>ses. Estos estudios encuentran que a Am<8e>rica Latina le ha ido relativamente mejor, no solo respecto a otras regiones sino igualmente en comparaci<97>n con crisis pasadas. Factores positivos ex<97>genos (como la r<87>pida recuperaci<97>n de la econom<92>a china) explican en parte este mejor desempe<96>o. Sin embargo, la lecci<97>n principal de la reciente crisis es que, por encima de la importancia de los factores ex<97>genos, el buen manejo macroecon<97>mico durante los a<96>os de auge econ<97>mico rindi<97> sus frutos. Posterior a las crisis de finales de los noventa y comienzos del 2000, los pa<92>ses de Am<8e>rica Latina reforzaron sus marcos de pol<92>tica macroecon<97>mica. Generaron as<92> mecanismos de contenci<97>n, lo que permiti<97> ejecutar pol<92>ticas anti-c<92>clicas tras la bancarrota de Lehman Brothers. En la actualidad, el marco de pol<92>tica elegido por la mayor<92>a de los pa<92>ses se encuentra basado en pol<92>ticas macroecon<97>micas prudentes y fundamentadas en reglas; sistemas financieros y mercados de capitales s<97>lidos; y una integraci<97>n a los mercados globales de bienes y de capitales. Esto contribuye a disminuir las vulnerabilidades de las econom<92>as de Am<8e>rica Latina (incluyendo el Paraguay) a eventuales choques externos. Debe reconocerse que existen ciertos aspectos que a<9c>n pueden ser mejorados. Por ejemplo, algunos pa<92>ses se beneficiar<92>an con una consolidaci<97>n fiscal gradual. Esto permitir<92>a acumular recursos que pueden ser necesarios para enfrentar una desaceleraci<97>n en el futuro y ayudar<92>a a preservar la credibilidad fiscal. Se<96>oras y se<96>ores El desaf<92>o clave para nuestros pa<92>ses es, por tanto, aprovechar las condiciones actuales a<9c>n favorables para consolidar los avances logrados en la <9c>ltima d<8e>cada y sentar las bases para un crecimiento sostenido bajo condiciones externas m<87>s adversas en el futuro. Para el banco central ello significa continuar implementado pol<92>ticas s<97>lidas, <87>giles y centradas en objetivos claros. As<92>, en la nueva coyuntura, la pol<92>tica monetaria deber<87> ser la primera l<92>nea de defensa frente a una materializaci<97>n de los riesgos. Sin embargo, lo anterior solo ser<87> posible si el marco de pol<92>tica monetaria es cre<92>ble y las expectativas de inflaci<97>n est<87>n bien ancladas. La estabilidad del poder de compra de nuestra moneda, presta a cumplir 70 a<96>os desde su creaci<97>n, ha sido una conquista de la sociedad. El mantenimiento de su valor es un desaf<92>o permanente, cuya responsabilidad recae principalmente sobre el banco central. Son harto conocidos los costos econ<97>micos y sociales de una inflaci<97>n elevada, la cual tiene efectos particularmente nocivos en la poblaci<97>n m<87>s pobre de un pa<92>s. Creo firmemente que un crecimiento sustentable, que traiga realmente beneficios a todos los estratos sociales, solo puede ser alcanzado con una inflaci<97>n baja, estable y predecible. <f2>nicamente en un escenario como este, se extiende el horizonte de planificaci<97>n de individuos y empresas y, consecuentemente, se concretan las inversiones que generan empleo, producci<97>n y renta. El combate a la inflaci<97>n ha sido, es y ser<87> la mejor contribuci<97>n de nuestro banco central para fomentar un crecimiento econ<97>mico sostenido con mayor equidad social. Para alcanzar este objetivo, continuaremos perfeccionando el esquema de pol<92>tica monetaria basado en metas de inflaci<97>n. El Banco Central del Paraguay ha adoptado desde el 2011, con resultados alentadores, este mecanismo para la gesti<97>n de su pol<92>tica monetaria. Con esto se han logrado tasas de inflaci<97>n m<87>s bajas y menos vol<87>tiles. Complementariamente seguiremos con un r<8e>gimen cambiario flexible, lo m<87>s coherente para un marco de metas de inflaci<97>n. En la nueva coyuntura ser<87> fundamental que el banco central siga manteniendo la flexibilidad cambiaria, que es un amortiguador de probada eficacia a choques externos. Al mismo tiempo, la autoridad monetaria tendr<87> la opci<97>n de intervenir en el mercado cambiario en circunstancias de incertidumbre o fuerte volatilidad del tipo de cambio, ya que ello puede tener efectos perniciosos sobre la econom<92>a. Por <9c>ltimo, debe reconocerse que una inflaci<97>n baja y estable no garantiza la estabilidad financiera, como lo demuestra la experiencia reciente de un buen n<9c>mero de econom<92>as avanzadas. En consecuencia, para evitar fluctuaciones abruptas de la actividad econ<97>mica y de los precios es esencial contar con sistemas financieros resistentes y eficientes. Un sistema financiero con estas caracter<92>sticas ser<87> esencial para afrontar exitosamente eventuales vientos en contra. En el Paraguay, las sucesivas crisis financieras de los a<96>os noventa dejaron inmensos costos para el fisco y la sociedad, postergando por muchos a<96>os el despegue de nuestra econom<92>a. Ante la nueva coyuntura, el banco central deber<87> seguir garantizando la calidad y eficiencia de la regulaci<97>n prudencial y de la supervisi<97>n de las instituciones financieras. La regulaci<97>n y supervisi<97>n de entidades financieras han experimentado grandes avances en los <9c>ltimos a<96>os, en particular al adoptarse un enfoque m<87>s basado en el riesgo. A pesar de ello, en t<8e>rminos de cumplimiento de los Principios B<87>sicos de Basilea para una Supervisi<97>n Bancaria Eficaz, nuestro marco regulatorio se encuentra a<9c>n por debajo del promedio de la regi<97>n. Existen actualmente restricciones o impedimentos legales que imposibilitan un mayor progreso en el dise<96>o de una regulaci<97>n m<87>s acorde con est<87>ndares internacionales. Es por ello que, para lograr un mayor avance, se requerir<87>n cambios en el marco jur<92>dico existente, modificaciones estas que ser<87>n realizadas en consulta con partes afectadas. El perfeccionamiento de la regulaci<97>n prudencial y de la supervisi<97>n del sistema financiero es un proceso continuo y sin fin. En este sentido, el banco central continuar<87> mejorando su aparato institucional y legal de monitoreo del sistema financiero nacional, con <8e>nfasis en asegurar la estabilidad financiera. La regulaci<97>n de las actividades bancarias y financieras debe igualmente promover un sistema financiero inclusivo. Esto tiene dos implicancias importantes. La primera (o micro) es social, una vez que la inclusi<97>n financiera contribuye a la reducci<97>n de las desigualdades sociales y al desarrollo econ<97>mico de cualquier pa<92>s. La segunda (o macro) est<87> asociada al hecho de que la inclusi<97>n financiera fortalece el principal canal de transmisi<97>n de la pol<92>tica monetaria, que es exactamente el sistema financiero. A pesar de avances recientes, nuestro pa<92>s se encuentra a<9c>n muy rezagado respecto al promedio internacional en t<8e>rminos de inclusi<97>n financiera. En consecuencia, el banco central implementar<87> una agenda extensa para fomentar la inclusi<97>n y la educaci<97>n financiera de la poblaci<97>n. Se<96>oras y se<96>ores El Banco Central del Paraguay es, indiscutiblemente, una instituci<97>n de excelencia, reconocida y respetada en el pa<92>s. No tengo la menor duda de que ese reconocimiento se debe primeramente a sus funcionarios, profesionales altamente calificados y comprometidos con las misiones legales e institucionales del banco. Nuestra pol<92>tica de recursos humanos seguir<87> apoy<87>ndose en los dos factores que han permitido nuestro suceso: la incorporaci<97>n de funcionarios de carrera a trav<8e>s de concursos p<9c>blicos de oposici<97>n y una pol<92>tica fuerte de capacitaci<97>n para el personal. Personalmente siento una gran satisfacci<97>n por poder volver a trabajar luego de 10 a<96>os con mis compa<96>eros y amigos del banco central. Mi anterior paso por la instituci<97>n me sirvi<97> mucho para apreciar y valorar la capacidad de los funcionarios. Compa<96>eros, ustedes son el mejor activo que tiene el BCP, cuento con todos ustedes para el <8e>xito en esta nueva gesti<97>n. En este momento de mi carrera profesional, me gustar<92>a recordar a algunas personas muy especiales. A mi padre, que si bien nos ha dejado f<92>sicamente cuando era peque<96>o, fue siempre una fuente inspiradora para m<92>. A mi madre, modelo de la guapeza de la mujer paraguaya, quien con su ejemplo de vida me ha mostrado el camino a seguir y para quien no existieron nunca obst<87>culos en la vida que sean imposibles de superar. A mis dos hijos, fuente inagotable de energ<92>a los d<92>as de semana hasta las once de la noche y los fines de semana desde las siete de la ma<96>ana, ellos son la alegr<92>a de nuestro hogar. A mi esposa, mi compa<96>era, mi amiga, quien sin ego<92>smo me acompa<96>a por los periplos determinados por mi vida profesional. Ella es el pilar de nuestro hogar, sin ella no ser<92>a nadie en lo profesional y mucho menos en lo personal. Para todos ellos mi gratitud eterna por todo lo que me han dado siempre y un les quiero mucho desde el fondo de mi coraz<97>n. Se<96>oras y se<96>ores Con la recuperaci<97>n de la econom<92>a americana se acaban paulatinamente los a<96>os extraordinarios de facilidad de financiaci<97>n y crecimiento garantizado que han vivido nuestros pa<92>ses durante la <9c>ltima d<8e>cada. El gran desaf<92>o es ahora preparar nuestras econom<92>as para enfrentar con <8e>xito un escenario externo m<87>s adverso. No es tiempo para la complacencia, pero tampoco para un pesimismo exagerado. Existen en el Paraguay condiciones macroecon<97>micas envidiables. En nuestro pa<92>s, la situaci<97>n de los bancos es firme, el marco de pol<92>tica monetaria es cre<92>ble, el nivel de cobertura de las reservas internacionales es adecuado y las finanzas p<9c>blicas son s<97>lidas. Tenemos todas las herramientas para seguir encaminando al Paraguay por una ruta de crecimiento sostenido, de pleno empleo y de progreso y bienestar para toda la poblaci<97>n. Manos a la obra. Muchas gracias. Asunci<97>n, 3 de octubre de 2013

Title: XI Regional Meeting of the Latin American Committee of the International Association of Deposit Insurers.
Subtitle: El Presidente del Banco Central del Paraguay (BCP), Carlos Fernandez Valdovinos dio apertura a la XI Reunin del Comit Regional de Amrica Latina de la Asociacin Internacional de Aseguradores de...
text: Members of the International Association of Deposit Insurers, Members of the Latin American Regional Committee, Representatives of the Private Financial System, Colleagues of the Central Bank of Paraguay, Ladies and gentlemen First of all, I would like to thank the Central Bank of Paraguay, in its capacity as administrator of the Deposit Guarantee Fund of our country, for its first time to host of a Meeting of the Latin American Regional Committee of the International Association of Deposit Insurers, this time called "The Role of Deposit Insurance in Times of Financial Stability and Normality". It is an honor and privilege to have the presence of all of you in our country and we give you the warmest welcome. Ladies and gentlemen I would like to reflect briefly on the role of deposit insurance schemes as a mechanism to promote financial stability in our countries. Deposit insurance, together with supervision, the provision of emergency liquidity funds and resolution schemes make up the typical financial safety net of our countries. These insurances strengthen the stability of the financial sector by mitigating uncertainty about the condition of banks, thereby reducing incentives for bank runs and limiting contagion between institutions. There are currently about 150 deposit insurance schemes around the world. Across countries, the role of insurance agencies varies significantly. At one extreme is the North American model, where the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) has supervisory powers and capabilities for the liquidation of troubled entities. At the other extreme, there is the so-called paybox model, where the powers of the agency are limited to the payment of depositors' claims in insured entities. Despite the diversity of practices, there is a common ground in all models: the existence of these insurances provide clarity, peace of mind and confidence to depositors, thus promoting financial stability. As emphasized in the Basic Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems, the main objectives of deposit insurance systems are to contribute to the stability of the financial system and to protect depositors. In order for these deposit insurance schemes to be credible, they must meet certain characteristics. First, they must have adequate coverage. To determine this level, the authorities should consider the distribution of deposits in the banking system and set a certain limit accordingly. For example, it could be a minimum level of coverage that protects 80 percent of depositors and about 20 percent of deposits. In practice, the average coverage per depositor is about twice the country's GDP per capita, but there is wide variability around this number. Second, they must provide timely payments. Insurance payments must be made in a timely manner to avoid disturbances in the payment system, preventing panics and bank runs. To this end, deposit insurance agencies must have adequate information in order to respond immediately in the event of a bankruptcy. A key issue in this context is the depositor's right of preference; i.e. giving to insured depositors and deposit insurance agencies privileged rights over the assets of a failing institution. This principle is not always included in national legislation. However, this collection privilege is highly positive as it facilitates a quick payment of insurance, increases the recovery of funds used by agencies and, consequently, reduces the total costs of having a deposit insurance scheme. Finally, deposit insurance schemes must have adequate funding. An ex ante financing system seems to be more appropriate in principle, since funds are built up gradually over time and before an event occurs. This type of funding strengthens the confidence of the private sector and increases financial stability, provided that risks are properly valued. Ex-post schemes, where funds must be provided by institutions once a bankruptcy is declared, could have pro-cyclical effects as the costs of the insurance system rise at a time when banks' balance sheets may be under pressure. A common element of all deposit insurance is the potential moral hazard problem in these schemes. As set out in the Basic Principles, it is necessary to reduce moral hazard by ensuring that the deposit insurance system has appropriate design elements. To this end, they must have limited coverage (so as not to induce market indiscipline and encourage risky behaviour); premiums that are adjusted for risk (so that there are no cross-subsidies between entities that end up benefiting those that take more risk) and strong supervision (which, complemented by adequate capital requirements, limit dangerous and unwise banking practices). Ladies and gentlemen In 2008, what would be the greatest economic and financial crisis of the last 80 years began. It highlighted the importance of having an effective deposit insurance scheme to guarantee national and global financial stability. During the crisis, depositor confidence was severely affected in some countries, mainly in Europe. In response to this uncertainty, the authorities decided to increase the coverage of their insurance schemes and, in some cases, went so far as to provide explicit sovereign guarantees for total deposits. These interventions entailed costs, in some cases very high, which have ultimately been borne by taxpayers. However, they were successful as they managed to limit uncertainty and avoid bank runs. The adoption of higher deposit hedges helped prevent investor panic in sovereign debt from being transmitted to financial institution depositors. This fact highlights the fundamental role that a deposit insurance scheme can play in preserving public confidence and ensuring financial stability. In Latin America, the effects of the 2008 global crisis on countries' financial systems have been marginal. This has not made it possible to test the effectiveness of existing insurance schemes in the region. Looking ahead, normalizing monetary conditions in the United States could lead to volatilities in some emerging economies. However, most of the financial systems in our region are prepared to face possible headwinds: the situation of the banks is firm and they have ample liquidity and capital buffers. However, this is no time for complacency. The authorities should take advantage of these times of relative stability and financial normality to further their deposit insurance schemes, which are crucial to ensuring a sound financial system that contributes to the economic and social development of our countries. In particular, alignment with existing regulations should ensure adequate and timely coverage of depositors; improve funding schemes so that contributions are based on the risk profile of institutions; help the implementation of efficient intervention protocols for financial institutions in trouble; and, contemplate the development of a massive dissemination campaign on deposit insurance. In Paraguay, the Deposit Guarantee Fund was established by Law No. 2.334 of 2003. This legislation established an explicit, limited, mandatory and onerous deposit guarantee regime. The fund, constituted with public and private funds, is administered by the Central Bank of Paraguay (BCP) as a separate patrimony. Currently it is It is analysing the draft reform of this law in order to adapt the regulations regarding deposit insurance and resolution of financial institutions to international best practices. The BCP Board firmly believes that resilient and efficient financial systems are essential for investments that generate employment, production and income to materialize. In turn, we believe that a properly designed deposit insurance scheme is critical to achieving these goals. Ladies and gentlemen I think we are all convinced that deposit insurance is a key piece of the financial safety net, which, in collaboration with others, seeks financial stability and the smooth functioning of the payment system. It is very difficult to think about the growth and economic development of our countries without a financial system that has these characteristics. This meeting represents a magnificent opportunity to discuss our region's recent advances in this area, and to deepen discussions on how to refine its structures and processes. I wish you a happy stay in our country and I am sure that the conclusions of the conference will be of great use to all of us. Thanks a lot. ------------o0o------------

Es un honor y privilegio contar con la presencia de todos ustedes en nuestro pa<92>s y les damos la m<87>s cordial bienvenida. Se<96>oras y Se<96>ores, Me gustar<92>a reflexionar brevemente sobre el rol de los esquemas de seguro de dep<97>sitos como mecanismo para promover la estabilidad financiera en nuestros pa<92>ses. Los seguros de dep<97>sitos, junto con la supervisi<97>n, la provisi<97>n de fondos de liquidez de emergencia y los esquemas de resoluci<97>n conforman la t<92>pica red de seguridad financiera de nuestros pa<92>ses. Estos seguros fortalecen la estabilidad del sector financiero al mitigar la incertidumbre sobre la condici<97>n de los bancos, reduciendo as<92> los incentivos de corridas bancarias y limitando el contagio entre instituciones. En la actualidad existen cerca de 150 esquemas de seguros de dep<97>sitos alrededor del mundo. A lo largo de los pa<92>ses, el rol de las agencias administradoras de estos seguros var<92>a significativamente. En un extremo se encuentra el modelo norteamericano, en donde la Corporaci<97>n Federal de Seguros de Dep<97>sitos (FDIC) posee facultades de supervisi<97>n y capacidades para la liquidaci<97>n de entidades en problemas. En el otro extremo, se encuentra el llamado modelo de caja de pagos o en ingl<8e>s <d2>paybox model<d3>, en donde las potestades de la agencia se limitan al pago de los reclamos de depositantes en las entidades aseguradas. A pesar de la diversidad de pr<87>cticas, existe una base com<9c>n en todos los modelos: la existencia de estos seguros proveen de claridad, tranquilidad y confianza a los depositantes, promoviendo de esa manera la estabilidad financiera. Como se recalca en los Principios B<87>sicos para Sistemas de Seguros de Dep<97>sitos Eficaces, los principales objetivos de los sistemas de seguro de dep<97>sitos son los de contribuir con la estabilidad del sistema financiero y proteger a los depositantes. A fin de que estos esquemas de seguro de dep<97>sitos sean cre<92>bles, los mismos deben reunir ciertas caracter<92>sticas. En primer lugar, ellos deben tener una cobertura adecuada. Para determinar dicho nivel, las autoridades deber<92>an considerar la distribuci<97>n de los dep<97>sitos en el sistema bancario y fijar en base a ello un determinado l<92>mite. Por ejemplo, podr<92>a ser un nivel m<92>nimo de cobertura que proteja a 80 por ciento de los depositantes y alrededor del 20 por ciento de los dep<97>sitos. En la pr<87>ctica, la cobertura promedio por depositante es alrededor de dos veces el PIB per c<87>pita del pa<92>s, pero existe amplia variabilidad alrededor de este n<9c>mero. En segundo lugar, los mismos deben proveer pagos oportunos. Los pagos de los seguros se deben realizar en tiempo y forma para evitar perturbaciones en el sistema de pagos, previniendo p<87>nicos y corridas bancarias. Para ello las agencias de seguro de dep<97>sitos deben contar con informaci<97>n adecuada a fin de responder inmediatamente en caso de una quiebra. Un tema clave en este contexto es el derecho de preferencia del depositante; es decir, dar a los depositantes asegurados y a las agencias de seguro de dep<97>sitos derechos privilegiados sobre los activos de una instituci<97>n en quiebra. Este principio no siempre est<87> incluido en las legislaciones nacionales. Sin embargo, este privilegio de cobro es altamente positivo ya que facilita un pago r<87>pido del seguro, aumenta la recuperaci<97>n de los fondos empleados por las agencias y, en consecuencia, reduce los costos totales de tener un esquema de seguros de dep<97>sitos. Por <9c>ltimo, los esquemas de seguro de dep<97>sitos deben contar con un fondeo adecuado. Un sistema de financiamiento ex ante pareciera ser m<87>s adecuado en principio, puesto que los fondos son constituidos gradualmente en el tiempo y antes de que ocurra un evento. Este tipo de fondeo fortalece la confianza del sector privado y aumenta la estabilidad financiera, toda vez que los riesgos sean adecuadamente valorados. Los esquemas ex post, donde los fondos deben ser prove<92>dos por las instituciones una vez declarada una quiebra, podr<92>an tener efectos pro-c<92>clicos ya que los costos del sistema de seguro aumentan en momentos en que los balances de los bancos pueden estar bajo presi<97>n. Un elemento com<9c>n de todos los seguros de dep<97>sitos es el potencial problema de riesgo moral en estos esquemas. Como establecido en los Principios B<87>sicos, es necesario reducir el riesgo moral cercior<87>ndose de que el sistema de seguros de dep<97>sitos cuente con elementos de dise<96>o apropiados. Para ello, los mismos deben contar con cobertura limitada (de modo a no inducir a la indisciplina del mercado y favorecer comportamientos riesgosos); primas que sean ajustadas por riesgo (para que no existan subsidios cruzados entre entidades que terminen beneficiando a las que toman m<87>s riesgo) y fuerte supervisi<97>n (que complementado con requerimientos de capital adecuados, limitan pr<87>cticas bancarias peligrosas y poco prudentes). Se<96>oras y se<96>ores En el a<96>o 2008 se iniciaba la que ser<92>a la mayor crisis econ<97>mica y financiera de los <9c>ltimos 80 a<96>os. La misma resalt<97> la importancia de contar con un esquema efectivo de seguros de dep<97>sitos para garantizar la estabilidad financiera nacional y global. Durante la crisis, la confianza de los depositantes se vio severamente afectada en algunos pa<92>ses, principalmente en Europa. En respuesta a esta incertidumbre, las autoridades decidieron incrementar la cobertura de sus esquemas de seguro y, en algunos casos, llegaron a proveer de garant<92>as soberanas expl<92>citas al total de los dep<97>sitos. Estas intervenciones conllevaron costos, en algunos casos muy elevados, que en <9c>ltima instancia han sido soportadas por los contribuyentes. Sin embargo, las mismas fueron exitosas ya que lograron limitar la incertidumbre y evitar las corridas bancarias. La adopci<97>n de coberturas m<87>s elevadas para los dep<97>sitos ayud<97> a prevenir que el p<87>nico de los inversionistas en deuda soberana sea transmitido a los depositantes de entidades financieras. Este hecho resalta el rol fundamental que un esquema de seguros de dep<97>sitos puede tener para preservar la confianza del p<9c>blico y asegurar la estabilidad financiera. En Am<8e>rica Latina, los efectos de la crisis global del 2008 sobre el sistema financiero de los pa<92>ses han sido marginales. Ello no ha permitido testar la eficacia de los esquemas de seguro existentes en la regi<97>n. Hacia el futuro, la normalizaci<97>n de las condiciones monetarias en los Estados Unidos podr<92>a ocasionar volatilidades en algunas econom<92>as emergentes. No obstante, la mayor<92>a de los sistemas financieros en nuestra regi<97>n est<87>n preparados para enfrentar eventuales vientos de frentes: la situaci<97>n de los bancos es firme y los mismos cuentan con amplios colchones de liquidez y capital. Sin embargo, no es tiempo para la complacencia. Las autoridades deber<92>an aprovechar estos tiempos de relativa estabilidad y normalidad financiera para ir perfeccionando sus esquemas de seguro de dep<97>sitos, cruciales para asegurar un sistema financiero s<97>lido que contribuya al desarrollo econ<97>mico y social de nuestros pa<92>ses. En particular, el ajuste a la normativa existente deber<92>a garantizar una cobertura adecuada y oportuna de los depositantes; mejorar los esquemas de fondeo para que las contribuciones se basen en el perfil de riesgo de las entidades; ayudar a la implementaci<97>n de protocolos de intervenci<97>n eficientes a las entidades financieras en problemas; y, contemplar el desarrollo de una campa<96>a de divulgaci<97>n masiva del seguro de dep<97>sitos. En el Paraguay, el Fondo de Garant<92>a de Dep<97>sitos fue creado por la Ley N<bc> 2.334 del a<96>o 2003. Esta legislaci<97>n estableci<97> un r<8e>gimen expl<92>cito, limitado, obligatorio y oneroso de garant<92>a de dep<97>sitos. El fondo, constituido con fondos p<9c>blicos y privados, es administrado por el Banco Central del Paraguay (BCP) como un patrimonio separado. Actualmente se est<87> analizando el proyecto de reforma de dicha ley a fin de adecuar la normativa referente a seguro de dep<97>sitos y resoluci<97>n de entidades financieras a las mejores pr<87>cticas internacionales. El Directorio del BCP cree firmemente que sistemas financieros resistentes y eficientes son fundamentales para que se materialicen las inversiones que generan empleo, producci<97>n y renta. A su vez, consideramos que un esquema de seguro de dep<97>sitos adecuadamente dise<96>ado es fundamental para el logro de estos objetivos. Se<96>oras y se<96>ores Creo que todos estamos convencidos de que el seguro de dep<97>sitos es una pieza clave de la red de seguridad financiera, que en colaboraci<97>n con las dem<87>s, procura la estabilidad financiera y el buen funcionamiento del sistema de pagos. Es muy dif<92>cil pensar en el crecimiento y desarrollo econ<97>mico de nuestros pa<92>ses sin un sistema financiero que tenga estas caracter<92>sticas. Esta reuni<97>n representa una magn<92>fica oportunidad para discutir los recientes avances de nuestra regi<97>n en el tema, y profundizar las discusiones acerca de c<97>mo perfeccionar sus estructuras y procesos. Les deseo a ustedes una feliz estad<92>a en nuestro pa<92>s y estoy seguro que las conclusiones de la conferencia ser<87>n de suma utilidad para todos nosotros. Muchas gracias. ------------o0o------------

Title: New member assumed the position on the BCP Board of Directors.
Subtitle: COMPROMETI SU ESFUERZO PARA IMPULSAR CAMBIOS EN MARCO JURDICO DEL BANCO CENTRAL DEL PARAGUAY En acto realizado esta maana en el Banco Central del Paraguay, con la presencia del titular del...
text: Minister of Finance, Mr. President of the Central Bank of Paraguay, Mr. Member of the Board of the Central Bank of Paraguay, Comrades of the Bank, Ladies and gentlemen It is a great honor and at the same time a commitment for me to assume the functions of Member of the Board of the Central Bank of Paraguay. A great honor, because from my early days in the Central Bank, as Manager of the Legal Unit, I noticed the extraordinary professional wealth of the officials of the institution, -at all levels- that made my work much more enjoyable and simple, and above all because I perceived in them fundamental values so uncommon today in our society, These include responsibility, honesty and respect for institutions. On the other hand, it is a commitment, because occupying the chair of Dr. Rolando Arrellaga will not be an easy task, -taking into account the great professional capacity and above all the human quality demonstrated by Rolando in the Board of Directors, which today gives prestige to the General Management of the Bank-. In addition, because  being the only lawyer  I will share tasks with excellent economists who share essential values, love this country, and are fully aware of the great pending task: to make Paraguay an increasingly better, more just and equitable country, where all its inhabitants enjoy economic and social well-being. What better proof of the above than the leadership recently demonstrated by the Central Bank, together with the Ministry of Finance, in the successful international issuance of sovereign bonds, in the exhausting and tireless effort deployed by representatives of the Bank in promoting the country abroad, and in the implementation of the most conducive measures so that ours is a model of a serious country where investments are respected and the country prevails. justice and equality over sectoral interests. The economic moment that Paraguay has to live in is unique, and I believe that the role of the Central Bank, and of all of us in that context, is fundamental. The maintenance of monetary stability and the strengthening of the financial sector will continue to be the main axes around which the necessary changes will be led to allow an increasing insertion of the country in the world. In this context, the Board of Directors will make my best efforts to promote the approval of the amendment of the Organic Law of the Central Bank of Paraguay and the Banking Law, modifications that are necessary to incorporate into the national regulatory plexus the latest international standards on monetary, financial and supervisory policy. and that aim at greater financial inclusion of the population within the framework of risk-based supervision. Likewise, the Board of Directors will be led by the normative and regulatory changes that are necessary for this purpose. I will contribute my legal vision and my experience in banking matters. In the same vein, we will support, together with the other national bodies, the implementation and enforcement of policies aimed at preventing money-laundering and the financing of terrorism, and we will promote international cooperation in this area. Likewise, I propose to give continuity to the preventive policy of judicial actions and settlement of differences by alternative means -which I applied from my position as Manager of the Legal Unit-, prioritizing the interests of the institution, without ignoring the rights of officials who may be compromised. Finally, and to conclude, I want to thank my family, especially my parents for teaching me from a very young age, -and demonstrating me by example-, the most important values of life; and to my wife and children, for being my daily supports, and for their patience and understanding. I cannot fail to mention my colleagues in the Management of the Legal Unit from whom I have learned a lot during these months, and with whom there has always been an atmosphere of dialogue, openness, transparency and camaraderie that are the characteristics that I want to continue maintaining in this new function, for which I put myself at the disposal of all.... I ask God to enlighten me in this important mission... Thanks a lot

Title: International experts gave lectures on best international financial practices at BCP.
Subtitle: CONFERENCIA ORGANIZADA CON EL FMI, BID, y BM Las experiencias de las crisis financieras mundiales y las razones que empujan a Paraguay para que redefina su legislacin financiera fueron algunos de...
text: Representatives of International Organizations, Representatives of the Financial System, civil society, students, Colleagues of the Central Bank of Paraguay, Ladies and Gentlemen, you are very welcome to this keynote speech. From the Central Bank of Paraguay (BCP) we have been carrying out, for several years, efforts to achieve a full consolidation of the national financial sector. For this, it is essential to implement the highest standards in terms of comprehensive risk management and corporate governance. This allows the financial system to function efficiently in good times and, at the same time, be sufficiently prepared to face the typical volatilities that arise in bad times. The successive financial crises of the nineties have been very costly, not only from the purely budgetary point of view but also from the social side. They became events that delayed our development process for several years. We have learned from these crises in the past and, since then, BCP has been perfecting its task in terms of implementing sound international regulatory practices and preventive supervision of financial institutions. These advances have been recognized by various multilateral organizations. During the last assessment mission of the Paraguayan financial system, the IMF and the World Bank highlighted that the level of compliance with our regulations with the Basel Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision had increased from 17% in 2005 to 63% in 2010. It has been a great advance, but clearly much remains to be done in terms of regulation and supervision to place us at the same level as the serious economies of the region. Today is the time to adapt our legal regime that is almost 20 years old. At the time, rigorous and more regulatory legislation was required to ensure unrestricted compliance without leaving anything to the discretion of either the BCP or the financial intermediaries. It was legislation prepared in a post-crisis situation, whose origins went back to the lack of sufficiently clear regulation that should have followed the liberalization process initiated in the early nineties. We currently have a different economy and a much larger and more modern financial system. For this reason, it is essential to grant greater regulatory powers to the BCP so that the content of its regulations adjusts when necessary to the dynamism of agile, demanding and competitive financial markets. Extremely detailed legislation is not consistent with the New times and, maintaining the status-quo, can be fertile ground for unwanted events to germinate in the near future. It is imperative to have more general legislation that allows financial regulation to be rapidly adapted to the dynamics of business in the sector and the risks inherent in it. The legal reforms that we are proposing propose the construction of an adequate environment conducive to the growth of the sector, but at the same time seek to ensure that this growth is rational and takes due account of possible risks. We have the best situation to carry out these changes. Such a reform is better done thoughtfully in quiet times than under the hurry and pressures typical of major financial crises. No one disputes the robustness and stability of the Paraguayan financial system and the BCP's permanent zeal to preserve these qualities. Today, the economic and financial scenario is propitious to introduce, reasoned and decisively, the best practices that will contribute to a greater expansion of the industry and, at the same time, strengthen the regulatory and supervisory role of the BCP. We are fully convinced of the need for the proposed changes, and we are determined to take them forward because we believe that they will be of benefit to ordinary citizens and allow our economy to continue on the path of higher, sustainable and inclusive economic growth. We thank the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank for their constant support through technical assistance and, on this occasion, for having facilitated the presence of our illustrious speakers. Thanks a lot!

Title: President of BCP spoke at the opening of the IX National Congress of ADEFI.
Subtitle: El titular del Banco Central del Paraguay, Carlos Fernndez Valdovinos, se dirigi a los participantes del IX Congreso Nacional de la Asociacin de Entidades Fiancieras del Paraguay...
text: ADEFI Annual Congress Thursday, November 27 Ladies and gentlemen: I thank ADEFI for inviting you to address a few words on the occasion of the Annual Congress of the same Paraguay's macroeconomic performance over the past decade has been characterized by a sustained expansion of economic activity, in a context of low, stable and predictable inflation, orderly fiscal accounts, an external sector in balance, gradually increasing monetary reserves and substantially low levels of indebtedness. In 2014, the economy continues to travel its path of expansion. The exceptions observed are punctual, mainly the case of electricity generation by binationals and the slight growth in agricultural production, behavior that is understandable, given the considerable expansion of this sector in the previous year. Likewise, a Less activity in sectors related to border trade and those hit by the scourge of smuggling. However, despite the more complicated global and regional environment, the Paraguayan economy is expected to grow by around 4% this year. Industry as a whole, construction and most branches of the service sector are evolving very satisfactorily this year and will allow our country's GDP growth to be one of the highest in the region. Inflation, meanwhile, has shown a downward trend since the end of the first half and would close the year between 3 and 4 percent. The increases observed at the beginning of the year, as a result of adjustments in administered prices, were gradually reduced, and year-on-year inflation, after reaching a rate of 7% in May, stood at 3.5% in October of this year. The BCP, since the end of 2013, foresaw inflationary pressures for the first months of this year, so, in a timely manner, it made the decision to reduce the Existing monetary impulse, increasing the monetary policy rate by 125 basis points between December 2013 and February of this year, to bring it to 6.75%, and thus give monetary policy a less expansionary profile. From March to November, the policy rate remained unchanged at that level. With these measures, inflationary pressures dissipated over the course of the year and have been consistent with the objective of ensuring that inflation converges to the annual target of 5% over the medium term. With this result, the BCP is once again fulfilling its commitment to maintain low, stable and predictable inflation. Moreover, since the implementation of the inflation targeting regime, the monetary authority has been able to keep price increases below the 5% target. We understand that these results allow strengthening the credibility of the institution, something that the BCP has been achieving as a result of its management in recent years. Likewise, this fact impels us to take on new challenges. to continue advancing towards similar standards in terms of methods and practices of other more advanced countries in the region. This good macroeconomic performance has been accompanied by an increasingly thriving and solid financial sector, fulfilling its fundamental role of channeling savings towards investment opportunities in the productive and household consumption sectors. The government also made placements of its instruments and captured resources that went to finance public works. The expansion of the financial system, as well as the greater commercial and financial integration with the rest of the world, have created new challenges for both the sector and the monetary authority, in terms of adapting the regulations that guarantee better regulation and supervision. In line with this evolution, the BCP has taken the initiative to modify and expand its Organic Charter and the General Law on Banks, Finance and Other Entities of Credit, with the purpose of having the legal instruments that allow adapting the financial system of Paraguay to the highest standards and best international practices of regulation and supervision. The central purpose of these amendments is to strengthen the risk-based supervisory scheme. We are convinced that an economy that seeks to maintain higher and sustained economic growth must have a central bank with greater capacity to act early and preventively. To do this, it must have the best tools of financial regulation and supervision, in order to ensure the solvency, stability and integrity of the financial system, characteristics that in turn are an indispensable condition for preserving the value of our currency, in accordance with our constitutional mandate. The reform of both laws must be consistent with each other and contemporary in their application. We consider that the current solid economic and financial scenario is propitious to introduce, Reasoned and decisively, these best practices will help maintain the healthy expansion of the financial industry. Such a proposal must be put forward in a premeditated manner and not by the constraint of circumstances and pressures typical of major financial crises. In addition, the modernization of this legal framework will contribute to improving the country risk rating, which implies in the future lower international funding costs for the government, for the financial system and for private companies. A stronger financial system is in everyone's interest, given the high economic, financial and social costs triggered by the financial crises that we have witnessed in past decades. We are confident that the testimony of our transparent management, together with the predisposition for the rational discussion of these issues of concern, will allow us to achieve the support of all affected sectors for the prompt implementation of the new legal framework. Finally, considering the experience of the last decade where the stability achieved by the financial system (through the joint efforts of financial agents, businessmen and directors and the regulator and supervisor of the system) has been one of the pillars of the growth of the Paraguayan economy, from the central bank we reaffirm our commitment to continue ensuring its expansion in an environment of stability and solvency. Thanks a lot.
