Title: Carlos Carvallo assumed as a new member of the BCP Board of Directors.
Subtitle: Esta maana a las 11 en el saln Auditorio del Banco Central del Paraguay asumi como nuevo Miembro Titular del Directorio del ente monetario, el Dr. Carlos Carballo Spalding, economista quien vuelve...
text: Many thanks to the President of the Central Bank Dr. Carlos Fernandez and the Minister of Finance, Dr. Santiago Pena, for their words. I would also like to thank my fellow Board Members, Ernesto Velazquez, Roland Holst and Rafael Lara, for their presence, as well as the directors of financial and insurance institutions, officials of the Central Bank, press workers, as well as colleagues and friends who are with us. All of you honor me today with your presence. I can see many familiar faces with whom we coincided in my time working at the Ministry of Finance, as well as colleagues with whom we share studies. It is a source of joy for me to meet you again, after a few years, and in these circumstances, and to have the possibility of working together with many of you right here, in the Central Bank itself, and with others, interacting in different areas. The President of the Republic, together with the Minister of Finance and the President of the Central Bank, have honored me by proposing me as a candidate for this position, a fact that makes me proud, but above all he commits me to give the greatest of my efforts in the performance of the function. Be sure that this will be the case. Likewise, I am grateful for the vote of confidence that the Honorable Chamber of Senators has given me, in giving its constitutional agreement so that I can, as of today, occupy the position of Full Member of the Board of Directors of the Central Bank. I want to highlight the institutional maturity with which, according to my perception, the whole process was developed. I particularly welcome the framework of seriousness, professionalism and respect, necessary conditions for solid institutions, which are the basis of a democratic Republic as shown. When President Carlos Fernandez contacted me and we talked about the possibility of being part of the Central Bank team as a Member of the Board of Directors, I told him that one of the aspects that motivated me most was to return to my country to join a team of excellence, and with which I am in full harmony with objectives. In particular, the Central Bank today has a President and a Board of Directors of great hierarchy, and officials of the highest technical level, a team that also included Dr. Pena, current Minister of Finance, who also developed an excellent management, and whose place I have to occupy today. And in a broader sense, the leadership for the achievement of the objectives of productive and social development in other areas of the State, also has internationally recognized experts. It is very encouraging the potential that this brings together, and the image that the country projects abroad. I hope I live up to it. I have accepted the challenge at a time when I feel that I have enough personal and professional maturity, but also enough energy to face greater challenges, and try to contribute the best of my efforts to the country. My family understood and shares the strength of this challenge and has been a fundamental support for me to be here today. Working in recent years from abroad, it is gratifying to perceive the international recognition that has gained the economic stability that has historically characterized our country, and particularly the growing respect for the advances in the management of its macroeconomy. The concern for economic stability has been adopting over time the character of "State policy" and I think that is an asset that is valued when looking at Paraguay. The Central Bank has been a key player in this performance. The results are visible and can be evaluated from different perspectives. That is, by contrasting these results with the commitments made, or by comparing them with those of other countries. Regarding the first perspective, since the inflation targeting scheme began to be implemented in May 2011, inflation has averaged 4.6%, systematically placing it within the target range. This, however, does not end in the BCP being an institution that fulfills the objectives publicly assumed, but that this is the beginning, it is the cornerstone on which credibility is built, a fundamental factor of institutional strength. As is known, under an inflation-targeting scheme such as the one followed by Paraguay, like a growing number of countries, the anchor of the system is the expectations of the agents. In Paraguay, these expectations have consistently been aligned with the Central Bank's goals, and this is evidence that the Bank has gained credibility. And this is not minor. Considering that in inflation issues the "self-fulfilling prophecies" are verified, to the extent that inflation expectations are located in the target environment, economic agents will operate based on that expectation and inflation will end up being located in the range without major costs for monetary policy. That is the result of a Central Bank that has long bet on building the credibility of its policies, and this is its main asset. I would add that inflation, in addition to being low  that is, located within the target range  has behaved more stably, that is, in terms of trajectory it has registered less volatility, which contributes to improving the perception of risk, reduces uncertainty, improves the business climate and favors investment. This behavior helps the head of entrepreneurs to change the chip from short to longer term. From another approach, if we place ourselves within our neighborhood, we are also very well positioned. In Brazil and Uruguay, inflation has been outside the target range for some time, Argentina and Venezuela do not implement the inflation targeting scheme and both have the highest rates in the region. Considering that we are the small partners of this neighborhood and are exposed to the same global and regional shocks as the neighbors, our result is not a coincidence. It was achieved because for many years we have been working in the right direction. On the other hand, looking ahead, we must be aware that the international context has changed. In a context in which the United States is gradually recovering, Europe is relatively stagnant, China announces a perhaps more than soft landing, and the region that does not grow and presents some indicators of macro stability that require monitoring, it is appreciated that the Central Bank of Paraguay has done its homework well, has built sufficient margins to face this international situation that is presented as less favorable. and therefore Paraguay can take off more than before the regional cycles. This is recognized by international reports and projections for the main economic variables of the country. The results, therefore, show that the scheme is effective and that it is being implemented well. Continuing along these lines requires maintaining a great deal of responsibility and prudence, but also having the right instruments to react quickly, and in that economic policy is fine. In addition, it should be added that this performance of inflation was achieved without sacrifice in terms of economic growth, as it emerges from the evolution of the level of activity and as suggested by the application of the Taylor rule. In this regard, it is enough to see the performance of Paraguay in recent years, which has been remarkable, growing 14.2% in 2013 and above 4% in 2014. The growth projection for this year remains firm, around its potential growth, in a context in which emerging economies and in particular those of Latin America begin to lose dynamism since 2012. In short, as economists like to say, macroeconomic variables are aligned with fundamentals. One aspect that I think is relevant to highlight is the possibility that the current monetary policy scheme has given us of having a flexible exchange rate, which can operate as an automatic stabilizer, making external and internal shocks less affected the real sector of the economy. The fact that the region has regained exchange rate flexibility in recent years is also good news. Additionally, the country's adequate level of public debt and the level of international reserves we have today provide us with enough slack to avoid unwanted volatilities and their negative effects on the economy. Turning to the financial field, it is observed that the sector has shown strong growth in recent years, As a dynamic and dynamic sector of our economy, the speed of innovations and technological changes that operate there force the regulatory entity to constantly modernize to accompany these progresses. The sophistication of the financial sector requires expertise to monitor it, and there is no doubt that the Central Bank has done much in terms of strengthening regulation and supervision, in terms of the specific training of its human capital, as well as the formation of supervisory bodies to support prevention. There have also been very important advances in terms of macroprudential policies, in line with international good practices. However, the development of this sector, critical for economic growth as a channeler of savings to investment, permanently challenges clear and timely rules, preventive supervision and institutional strength. The discussion that is being processed today about the adequacy of the Banking Law and the Organic Charter goes in that direction, in the encounter of international standards in terms of supervision, and it is taking place at an opportune moment, when the economy is firm and stable as now. Likewise, based on a stable financial system, it should aim to promote financial inclusion, with the dual purpose of contributing to the reduction of social inequalities but, in addition, of strengthening the main channel of transmission of monetary policy, contributing to its effectiveness. The financial education work being carried out by the Central Bank is aimed at this objective. Of course, important challenges remain for economic policy, but with macroeconomic stability  which is a necessary condition, although not sufficient under control, and with a real sector that is still dynamic  it is possible to focus on the most structural and strategic challenges, which require strong commitment from different actors at the national level and time to see the results. The country urgently needs to continue working tirelessly on improving education, health, infrastructure, diversification and productive inclusion, systemic competitiveness, institutions in its broad sense, among other issues that allow us to increase our sustained growth in the long term, with social inclusion and equity, in short, promote greater welfare of our population. Undoubtedly, progress is being made regarding, for example, the diversification of the productive matrix and the opening of new markets. The dynamism of non-traditional sectors whose demand sustains economic growth in the face of the fall in commodity prices provides some indications of how changes in the pattern of production and employment can contribute to mitigating the social effects of changes in the economic cycle, but there is still a long way to go. In our country there are still significant levels of poverty and exclusion, and these are not only fought with growth and economic stability, but with policies focused on development, based on a much broader and multidimensional approach. The challenges are great, but very significant progress is also being made in that direction. In this context, monetary policy must contribute to this objective, be aligned. Economics textbooks teach us about the social advantages of low and stable inflation, such as the reduction of menu costs, the deepening of the capital market, the facilitation for the evaluation of projects and therefore investment, among others. What is often not mentioned in manuals written in developed countries is the importance for competitiveness. If inflation in dollars is higher than that recorded by our competition, we become more expensive, we stay out of the markets and we reduce the capacity to create quality jobs. For a small country with low purchasing power, growth depends on insertion in external markets - if possible with more sophisticated demands - that demand quality jobs. In this framework, low and stable inflation does not guarantee anything, but it is a prerequisite. The understandable demand of society for tangible and immediate results can lead to short-term temptations, risking the economic stability that has taken us a long time to build. We must take care of this asset as a treasure, and continue to bet, as has been done, on the articulation between economic policy and social policies, which allows us to move towards true socio-economic development. The fight against inflation and the zealous care of the stability and health of the financial system is the greatest contribution that the Central Bank can make to society, in the search for sustained growth with greater social equity. I would also like to highlight the important degree of coordination between fiscal and monetary policy observed in our country. The Central Bank and the Ministry of Finance work together, and that which seems trivial, is sometimes not common when observing the reality in other countries. Maintaining this line not only reduces the costs of macroeconomic policies in terms of real variables, but also provides accurate signals that local and international agents clearly decode, influencing their decisions, particularly investment decisions. In this context, I consider it important to highlight the importance of the Fiscal Responsibility Law, and the commitment reiterated by the Minister of Finance in its fulfillment. This is an extremely valuable instrument for creating the conditions for a truly counter-cyclical economic policy. Finally, I would like to conclude these words by reiterating my special thanks to Dr. Carlos Fernandez, President of the Central Bank, for having trusted that my years of experience in the exercise of the profession in the country and in international organizations in recent years, as well as the profile of my academic training, can contribute and complement the board that today leads the Central Bank. And to several very dear friends, many present here today, who have encouraged me to pack my bags and return to the homeland. I'm happy it was. As of today, I am joining an institution of excellence, recognized and respected in the country, whose reputation is due, first of all, to the professional quality of its officials. For my part, you have the most absolute commitment that I will fully adhere to strict compliance with the rules that govern the operation of this Institution, guided by the honesty and ethics that must govern our role as public servants at all times. I ask God to illuminate this new path that together with you I begin to undertake. Thank you all very much
text_original: Muchas gracias al presidente del Banco Central Dr. Carlos Fern<87>ndez y al Ministro de Hacienda, Dr. Santiago Pe<96>a, por sus palabras. Quisiera agradecer, adem<87>s, la presencia de mis colegas Miembros del Directorio, Ernesto Vel<87>zquez, Roland Holst y Rafael Lara, as<92> como de los se<96>ores Directivos de entidades financieras y de seguros, funcionarios del Banco Central, trabajadores de la prensa, adem<87>s de los colegas y amigos que nos acompa<96>an. Todos ustedes me honran hoy con su presencia. Puedo ver muchas caras conocidas con quienes coincidimos en mi <8e>poca de trabajo en el Ministerio de Hacienda, as<92> como de colegas con los que compartimos estudios. Es un motivo de alegr<92>a para m<92> volver a encontrarlos, despu<8e>s de algunos a<96>os, y en estas circunstancias, y de tener la posibilidad de trabajar junto con muchos de ustedes aqu<92> mismo, en el propio Banco Central, y con otros, interactuando en diferentes <87>reas. El se<96>or Presidente de la Rep<9c>blica, junto al Ministro de Hacienda y al Presidente del Banco Central me han honrado al proponerme como candidato para este cargo, hecho que me enorgullece, pero sobretodo me compromete a dar el mayor de mis esfuerzos en el desempe<96>o de la funci<97>n. Tengan por cierto que as<92> ser<87>. Asimismo, agradezco el voto de confianza que me ha otorgado la Honorable C<87>mara de Senadores, al dar su acuerdo constitucional para que pueda, a partir de hoy, ocupar el cargo de Miembro Titular del Directorio del Banco Central. Quiero destacar, la madurez institucional con la que, seg<9c>n mi percepci<97>n, fue desarrollado todo el proceso. Celebro especialmente el marco de seriedad, profesionalismo y respeto, condiciones necesarias para instituciones s<97>lidas, que son la base de una Rep<9c>blica democr<87>tica como la muestra. Cuando el Presidente Carlos Fern<87>ndez me contact<97> y conversamos acerca de la posibilidad de formar parte del equipo del Banco Central en calidad de Miembro del Directorio, le manifest<8e> que uno de los aspectos que m<87>s me motivaba era volver a mi pa<92>s para integrar un equipo de excelencia, y con el que me encuentro en plena sinton<92>a de objetivos. En particular, el Banco Central cuenta hoy con un Presidente y un Directorio de gran jerarqu<92>a, y funcionarios de alt<92>simo nivel t<8e>cnico, equipo que adem<87>s integr<97> el Dr. Pe<96>a, actual Ministro de Hacienda, quien tambi<8e>n desarroll<97> una excelente gesti<97>n, y cuyo lugar hoy me toca ocupar. Y en un sentido m<87>s amplio, la conducci<97>n para el logro de los objetivos de desarrollo productivo y social en otras <87>reas del Estado, cuenta tambi<8e>n con expertos reconocidos internacionalmente. Es muy alentador el potencial que as<92> se re<9c>ne, y la imagen que proyecta el pa<92>s hacia el exterior. Espero yo estar a la altura. He aceptado el desaf<92>o en un momento en que siento que cuento con la suficiente madurez personal y profesional, pero tambi<8e>n con la suficiente energ<92>a como para enfrentar retos mayores, e intentar aportar el mejor de mis esfuerzos al pa<92>s. Mi familia entendi<97> y comparte la fuerza de este desaf<92>o y ha sido un soporte fundamental para que yo est<8e> hoy aqu<92>. Trabajando los <9c>ltimos a<96>os desde el extranjero, es gratificante percibir el reconocimiento internacional que ha ganado la estabilidad econ<97>mica que hist<97>ricamente ha caracterizado a nuestro pa<92>s, y particularmente el creciente respeto por los avances en lo que refiere al manejo de su macroeconom<92>a. La preocupaci<97>n por la estabilidad econ<97>mica ha ido adoptando en el transcurso del tiempo car<87>cter de "pol<92>tica de Estado" y creo que ese es un activo que se valora cuando se observa a Paraguay. El Banco Central ha sido protagonista clave en este desempe<96>o. Los resultados est<87>n a la vista y se los puede evaluar desde distintas perspectivas. Esto es, contrastando esos resultados con los compromisos asumidos, o compar<87>ndolos con los de otros pa<92>ses. Respecto a la primera perspectiva, desde que se comenz<97> a implementar el esquema de metas de inflaci<97>n a partir de mayo de 2011, la inflaci<97>n ha sido en promedio de 4.6%, ubic<87>ndose sistem<87>ticamente dentro del rango meta. Esto, sin embargo, no termina en que el BCP es una instituci<97>n que cumple los objetivos asumidos p<9c>blicamente, sino que este es el comienzo, es la piedra angular sobre la que se construye la credibilidad, factor fundamental de la fortaleza institucional. Como es sabido, bajo un esquema de metas de inflaci<97>n como el que sigue Paraguay, al igual que un creciente n<9c>mero de pa<92>ses, el ancla del sistema son las expectativas de los agentes. En Paraguay, estas expectativas sistem<87>ticamente han estado alineadas con las metas del Banco Central, y esto es evidencia de que el Banco ha ganado credibilidad. Y esto no es menor. Considerando que en temas de inflaci<97>n se verifica aquello de las "profec<92>as autocumplidas", en la medida que las expectativas de inflaci<97>n se ubiquen en el entorno de la meta, los agentes econ<97>micos operar<87>n en base a esa expectativa y la inflaci<97>n terminar<87> ubic<87>ndose en el rango sin mayores costos para la pol<92>tica monetaria. Ese es el resultado de un Banco Central que apost<97> durante mucho tiempo a la construcci<97>n de la credibilidad de sus pol<92>ticas, y este es su principal activo. Agregar<92>a que la inflaci<97>n, adem<87>s de baja -esto es, ubicada al interior del rango objetivo-, se ha comportado de manera m<87>s estable, es decir, en t<8e>rminos de trayectoria ha registrado menor volatilidad, lo cual contribuye a mejorar la percepci<97>n de riesgo, disminuye la incertidumbre, mejora el clima de negocios y favorece la inversi<97>n. Este comportamiento contribuye a que la cabeza de los emprendedores pueda cambiar el chip de corto a m<87>s largo plazo. Desde otro enfoque, si nos situamos dentro de nuestro barrio, tambi<8e>n nos encontramos muy bien posicionados. En Brasil y Uruguay la inflaci<97>n se ha encontrado durante alg<9c>n tiempo fuera de rango meta, Argentina y Venezuela no implementan el esquema de metas de inflaci<97>n y ambos tienen las tasas m<87>s altas de la regi<97>n. Considerando que somos los socios peque<96>os de este barrio y estamos expuestos a los mismos choques globales y regionales que los vecinos, nuestro resultado no es una casualidad. Se logr<97> porque hace muchos a<96>os se viene trabajando en la direcci<97>n correcta. Por otra parte, mirando para adelante, debemos ser conscientes que el contexto internacional ha cambiado. En un marco en que Estados Unidos se recupera gradualmente, Europa est<87> relativamente estancada, China nos anuncia un aterrizaje tal vez m<87>s que suave, y la regi<97>n que no crece y presenta algunos indicadores de estabilidad macro que requieren seguimiento, se aprecia que el Banco Central de Paraguay ha hecho bien los deberes, ha construido m<87>rgenes suficientes para enfrentar esta coyuntura internacional que se presenta como menos favorable, y por ello Paraguay puede despegarse m<87>s que antes de los ciclos regionales. Esto es reconocido por informes y proyecciones internacionales para las principales variables econ<97>micas del pa<92>s. Los resultados, por tanto, muestran que el esquema es efectivo y que se est<87> implementando bien. Continuar en esta l<92>nea requiere mantener mucha responsabilidad y prudencia, pero tambi<8e>n disponer de los instrumentos adecuados para reaccionar r<87>pidamente, y en eso la pol<92>tica econ<97>mica est<87> bien. Adem<87>s, cabe agregar que este desempe<96>o de la inflaci<97>n fue logrado sin sacrificio en t<8e>rminos de crecimiento econ<97>mico, tal como surge a partir de la evoluci<97>n del nivel de actividad y como sugiere la aplicaci<97>n de la regla de Taylor. Al respecto, basta ver el desempe<96>o de Paraguay en los <9c>ltimos a<96>os, que ha sido notable, creciendo 14,2% en 2013 y por encima del 4% en el 2014. La proyecci<97>n de crecimiento para este a<96>o se mantiene firme, en torno a su crecimiento potencial, en un marco en que las econom<92>as emergentes y en particular las de Latinoam<8e>rica comienzan a perder dinamismo ya desde 2012. En definitiva, como nos gusta decir a los economistas, las variables macroecon<97>micas est<87>n alineadas a los fundamentos. Un aspecto que me parece relevante resaltar, es la posibilidad que nos ha dado el actual esquema de pol<92>tica monetaria de disponer de un tipo de cambio flexible, que pueda operar como estabilizador autom<87>tico, haciendo que los choques externos e internos afecten menos al sector real de la econom<92>a. El hecho de que la regi<97>n en los <9c>ltimos a<96>os haya recuperado la flexibilidad cambiaria tambi<8e>n es una buena noticia. Adicionalmente, el adecuado nivel de endeudamiento p<9c>blico del pa<92>s y el nivel de reservas internacionales del que hoy disponemos, nos brindan la suficiente holgura como para evitar volatilidades no deseadas y sus efectos negativos sobre la econom<92>a. Pasando al <87>mbito financiero, se observa que el sector ha mostrado un fuerte crecimiento en los <9c>ltimos a<96>os, Como sector din<87>mico y dinamizador de nuestra econom<92>a, la rapidez de las innovaciones y los cambios tecnol<97>gicos que all<92> operan obligan al ente regulador a modernizarse constantemente para acompa<96>ar estos progresos. La sofisticaci<97>n del sector financiero requiere expertise para su seguimiento, y no cabe duda que el Banco Central ha hecho mucho en t<8e>rminos de fortalecimiento de la regulaci<97>n y la supervisi<97>n, en lo que refiere a la formaci<97>n espec<92>fica de su capital humano, as<92> como la conformaci<97>n de instancias de supervisi<97>n que permitan apoyar la prevenci<97>n. Tambi<8e>n ha habido avances muy importantes en lo que refiere a pol<92>ticas macroprudenciales, en la l<92>nea de las buenas pr<87>cticas internacionales. No obstante, el desarrollo de este sector, cr<92>tico para el crecimiento econ<97>mico en tanto canalizador de ahorro a inversi<97>n, desaf<92>a permanentemente a tener reglas claras y oportunas, supervisi<97>n preventiva y fortaleza institucional. La discusi<97>n que hoy se est<87> procesando acerca de la adecuaci<97>n de la Ley de Bancos y de la Carta Org<87>nica va en esa direcci<97>n, al encuentro de est<87>ndares internacionales en materia de supervisi<97>n, y se est<87> dando en un momento oportuno, cuando la econom<92>a se muestra firme y estable como ahora. Asimismo, a partir de un sistema financiero estable, se debe apuntar a promover la inclusi<97>n financiera, con el doble prop<97>sito de contribuir a la disminuci<97>n de las desigualdades sociales pero, adem<87>s, de fortalecer el principal canal de transmisi<97>n de la pol<92>tica monetaria, contribuyendo a su efectividad. Los trabajos de educaci<97>n financiera que viene desarrollando el Banco Central apuntan a ese objetivo. Por supuesto que persisten importantes desaf<92>os para la pol<92>tica econ<97>mica, pero con la estabilidad macroecon<97>mica -que es una condici<97>n necesaria, aunque no suficiente bajo control, y con un sector real todav<92>a din<87>mico, se habilita poner foco en los desaf<92>os m<87>s estructurales y estrat<8e>gicos, que requieren fuerte compromiso de diferentes actores a nivel nacional y tiempo para ver los resultados. El pa<92>s necesita imperiosamente seguir trabajando sin descanso sobre la mejora en la educaci<97>n, la salud, la infraestructura, la diversificaci<97>n e inclusi<97>n productiva, la competitividad sist<8e>mica, la institucionalidad en su sentido amplio, entre otros temas que nos permitan aumentar nuestro crecimiento sostenido en el largo plazo, con inclusi<97>n social y equidad, en s<92>ntesis, promover un mayor bienestar de nuestra poblaci<97>n. Sin dudas se est<87>n haciendo avances en lo que refiere, por ejemplo, a la diversificaci<97>n de la matriz productiva y la apertura de nuevos mercados. El dinamismo de sectores no tradicionales cuya demanda sostiene el crecimiento econ<97>mico ante la ca<92>da en el precio de los commodities, brinda algunos indicios de c<97>mo los cambios en el patr<97>n de producci<97>n y empleo pueden contribuir a mitigar los efectos sociales de los cambios en el ciclo econ<97>mico, pero falta todav<92>a un largo camino por recorrer. En nuestro pa<92>s todav<92>a persisten niveles de pobreza y exclusi<97>n importantes, y estos no se combaten s<97>lo con crecimiento y estabilidad econ<97>mica, sino con pol<92>ticas enfocadas al desarrollo, a partir de un abordaje mucho m<87>s amplio y multidimensional. Los desaf<92>os son grandes pero tambi<8e>n se est<87>n haciendo avances muy significativos en esa direcci<97>n. En este marco, la pol<92>tica monetaria debe contribuir a este objetivo, estar alineada. Los manuales de econom<92>a nos ense<96>an sobre las ventajas sociales de una inflaci<97>n baja y estable, tales como la disminuci<97>n de los costos de men<9c>, la profundizaci<97>n del mercado de capitales, la facilitaci<97>n para la evaluaci<97>n de proyectos y por tanto la inversi<97>n, entre otros. Lo que no mencionan muchas veces los manuales escritos en los pa<92>ses desarrollados, es la importancia para la competitividad. Si la inflaci<97>n en d<97>lares es m<87>s alta que la que registra nuestra competencia, nos encarecemos, quedamos fuera de los mercados y disminuimos la capacidad de creaci<97>n de empleos de calidad. Para un pa<92>s peque<96>o y de bajo poder adquisitivo, el crecimiento depende de la inserci<97>n en mercados externos - en lo posible con demandas m<87>s sofisticadas - que exijan empleos de calidad. En este marco, una inflaci<97>n baja y estable no garantiza nada, pero es pre-requisito. La entendible demanda de la sociedad por resultados tangibles e inmediatos, puede conducir a tentaciones cortoplacistas, arriesgando la estabilidad econ<97>mica que nos ha costado mucho tiempo construir. Debemos cuidar este activo como un tesoro, y seguir apostando, como se ha venido haciendo, a la articulaci<97>n entre la pol<92>tica econ<97>mica y las pol<92>ticas sociales, que permita avanzar hacia un verdadero desarrollo socio-econ<97>mico. El combate a la inflaci<97>n y el celoso cuidado de la estabilidad y salud del sistema financiero es la mayor contribuci<97>n que el Banco Central puede hacer a la sociedad, en la b<9c>squeda de un crecimiento sostenido con mayor equidad social. No quiero dejar de destacar tambi<8e>n el importante grado de coordinaci<97>n entre la pol<92>tica fiscal y la monetaria que se observa en nuestro pa<92>s. El Banco Central y el Ministerio de Hacienda trabajan articuladamente, y eso que parece trivial, a veces no es com<9c>n cuando se observa la realidad en otros pa<92>ses. Mantener esta l<92>nea, no s<97>lo reduce los costos de las pol<92>ticas macroecon<97>micas en t<8e>rmino de variables reales, sino que brinda se<96>ales certeras que los agentes locales e internacionales decodifican con claridad, incidiendo en sus decisiones, en particular, en las de inversi<97>n. En este contexto, considero relevante resaltar la importancia de la Ley de Responsabilidad Fiscal, y del compromiso reiterado por el Ministro de Hacienda en su cumplimiento. Este es un instrumento sumamente valioso para generar las condiciones de una pol<92>tica econ<97>mica verdaderamente anti-c<92>clica. Finalmente, quiero concluir estas palabras reiterando mi especial agradecimiento al Dr. Carlos Fern<87>ndez, Presidente del Banco Central, por haber confiado en que mis a<96>os de experiencia en el ejercicio de la profesi<97>n en el pa<92>s y en organismos internacionales en los <9c>ltimos a<96>os, as<92> como el perfil de mi formaci<97>n acad<8e>mica, pueden contribuir y complementar al directorio que hoy conduce el Banco Central. Y a varios amigos muy queridos, muchos hoy aqu<92> presentes, que me han alentado a hacer las valijas y volver a la patria. Estoy feliz que as<92> haya sido. Estoy a partir de hoy integr<87>ndome a una instituci<97>n de excelencia, reconocida y respetada en el pa<92>s, cuya reputaci<97>n se debe, en primer lugar, a la calidad profesional de sus funcionarios. De mi parte, cuenten con el compromiso m<87>s absoluto de que me desempe<96>ar<8e> apegado plenamente al cumplimiento estricto de las normas que rigen el funcionamiento de esta Instituci<97>n, obrando guiado por la honestidad y la <8e>tica que debe regir en todo momento nuestro rol de servidores p<9c>blicos. Le pido a Dios que ilumine este nuevo camino que junto con ustedes comienzo a emprender. Muchas gracias a todos

text: Commemorative Coin - Visit of Pope Francis Opening Remarks . Mr. President of the Republic, Horacio Cartes Jara, . Mr. Vice-President of the Republic, Juan Eudes Afara, . Monsignor Edmundo Valenzuela, Archbishop of Asuncion, . Dear Ministers of the Executive Power, . Members present, . Ambassadors and Representatives of friendly countries, . Ecclesiastical, Civil and Military Authorities present, . Ladies and gentlemen. The visit of Pope Francis to our country is a fact that, without a doubt, revives the values and civic virtues of us Paraguayans. With his witness of life, Pope Francis is a person from whom we have much to learn and, in just two years of pontificate, he has already left us abundant teachings, especially of humility and openness. Above all, the fact that he is very close to our land connects us even more to his testimonies. His reflections and actions go far beyond the strictly religious, encompassing considerations on social, political, environmental and even economic aspects. As an example, in one of his reflections he told us: "The economy, as the word itself indicates, should be the art of achieving an adequate administration of the common home, which is the whole world." In simple words, Pope Francis tells us that, while all growth is good, it should be based on a healthy balance. That is, it is not enough to grow or accumulate wealth every year, but we must do it at a sustainable pace so that society does not run the risk of assuming very high costs in the medium and long term as a result of this greater growth. One of these potential costs is the overexploitation of natural resources, which endangers the life of the planet since the world economy cannot grow beyond the carrying capacity of the ecosystem. But in addition, there may be a high social cost. Pope Francis rightly emphasizes that "human rights are not only violated with terrorist acts, repressions or murders, but also with unjust economic structures that generate great inequalities." Growth that widens social gaps and generates precarious jobs is not satisfactory. Economic growth should be sustainable by reducing both poverty and inequality or the gap between the richest and the poorest. But a more egalitarian society is not only morally desirable, it makes sense from a strictly economic point of view. A recent IMF study highlights that economic inequality reduces growth potential, so if you want to revitalize economic activity it is more useful to promote the progress of the lower income strata of society. Over the past ten years, Latin America (including Paraguay) has transformed the region's socioeconomic situation, increasing its middle class to unprecedented levels, reducing inequality and lifting millions out of poverty. While we have begun to walk the right path, there is still much to be done. The current context of global economic slowdown and less favorable external conditions for our products create new challenges. No more tailwinds. The design of adequate public policies that promote growth and well-being for all will be fundamental in the new situation. But this "revolutionary" Pope preaches not only with his words, but also with his actions. One of his first changes within the Roman curia was the creation of the Vatican Secretariat for the Economy in order to rationalize spending and intensify surveillance in Vatican finances. What an example! Without being a doctor in economics, the Pope understood very well that having public finances in order and healthy and transparent fiscal accounts is an unavoidable initial condition for any country or state, including the Vatican. Likewise, Pope Francis, by his simple example, reminds those of us in public administration that we are there to serve. I remember that unforgettable moment after the white smoke and the exciting "Habemus Papa". We all expected the new Supreme Pontiff to appear. Dressed in an intense red and gold, following the Roman tradition. However, we could see a simple man with an austere white cassock and no stole coming out on the balcony. At that moment we realized that something was going to change. In fact, in the celebration held at the beginning of his pontificate, he mentioned that "Let us never forget that true power is service." It is their way of saying "I am here to serve you" and showing that the important thing is not those who exercise power conjuncturally, but the people. Exercising that power from the government implies a greater responsibility towards the attention of the weakest and most needy. This was highlighted by the Supreme Pontiff saying: "It is imperative that the rulers and the financial powers raise their eyes and broaden their perspectives, that they ensure that there is decent work, education and health care for all citizens." We policy decision-makers must remember his example every day and be sensitive to people's needs and not lose sight of the fact that, with our actions, we must seek greater social welfare for all, without distinction. Another of Pope Francis' teachings, which is particularly important for us Paraguayans, refers to the attitude or bad habit of focusing many times on the negative instead of the positive. A few days ago, we were proud of how our beloved albirroja was gradually overcoming the obstacles to be placed in the semifinal of the Copa America. But that semifinal did not have the outcome we all expected. As the game went on, many automatically transformed that pride into frustration and negativism, detracting from the achievements that our compatriots had already achieved and that had left the name of our country high again. It reminded me of what the Pope once said to a group of communicators: "Of course sometimes negative things happen, but often we manipulate the facts and focus more on the negative than the positive." Low self-esteem influences the ability to develop as a nation and to progress socially. It is time that we put aside the "auto-boycott" (as some call it) that we Paraguayans often do. The recent stability and economic development of Paraguay leave more than one speechless and the numbers speak for themselves. The digital newspaper USA Hispanic echoed a few days ago a comment by a university professor and political analyst. It pointed out that "Paraguay does not need external enemies if we shoot each other ourselves. There is no dividing line between the sound criticism we all can and must make of our rulers and the current self-destruction we witness daily." Ladies and gentlemen, although we lost the semi-final against Argentina, we are world champions to control inflation according to the World Economic Forum. In addition, I tell you that we did reach the final of the Copa America, since we are vice champions of the continent in having the lowest public debt and we are only surpassed by Chile. Of course, much remains to be done to be the country we all want. But change is only possible through critical and demanding attitudes, together with committed and responsible actions by all. Let us Paraguayans learn to look at Paraguay with the same eyes as many foreigners. This includes not only risk rating agencies, multilateral organizations or international investors, but any casual visitor who is surprised by the progress that has recently been made in the country. Pope Francis himself has a high regard for Paraguay and its inhabitants. At the time, he recalled how our people knew how to overcome a devastating and unjust war. Much of it thanks to the Paraguayan woman, the most glorious in all of America. I do not forget his words "I wish that one day the Nobel Prize Committee would award the Nobel Prize to the Paraguayan woman!" Following his teachings, let us then value the progress we have made as a society, let us walk together the path of development of our nation, let us learn to make objective and constructive criticisms. Only in this way will it be possible to reach the country that all Paraguayans want. The Pope's visit is a historic event that will endure in the memory of all Paraguayans. Our Guarani currency, from its very name, represents the diversity and richness of our culture and in it is embodied our essence as Paraguayans. The Central Bank considers that the minimum contribution it could make to honor our illustrious visitor is through one of the forms of expression of our society: the guarani, our national currency. Thus, the BCP adheres to the great joy and hope of Paraguayans before the visit of His Holiness and has put all its effort into the minting of a commemorative coin alluding to the visit of Pope Francis. This coin is very simple, following the teachings of the one who pays homage. On the obverse is printed the engraving of the face of Pope Francis with a cross and the inscription "Francis blesses Paraguay" at the top. At the bottom is written "Messenger of joy and peace" in the language that most identifies us, Guarani. On the reverse it bears an illustration of our national coat of arms with the inscription "Republica del Paraguay" at the top and "1 Guarani" at the bottom. Precisely "Messenger of joy and peace" is the nickname that we Paraguayans gave to Pope Francis as thanks for his visit to the country. Coincidentally, this messenger comes to share his joy and peace with a country that, according to the Gallup pollster, is the happiest in the world. The issuance of this currency represents the simple way through which the Central Bank of Paraguay pays a well-deserved tribute and welcomes Pope Francis. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Moneda Conmemorativa - Visita del Papa Francisco Palabras de Apertura . Se<96>or Presidente de la Rep<9c>blica, Horacio Cartes Jara, . Se<96>or Vice-Presidente de la Republica, Juan Eudes Afara, . Monse<96>or Edmundo Valenzuela, Arzobispo de Asunci<97>n, . Se<96>ores Ministros del Poder Ejecutivo, . Se<96>ores Parlamentarios presentes, . Se<96>ores Embajadores y Representantes de pa<92>ses amigos, . Autoridades Eclesi<87>sticas, Civiles y Militares presentes, . Se<96>oras y Se<96>ores. La visita del Papa Francisco a nuestro pa<92>s constituye un hecho que, sin lugar a dudas, reaviva los valores y las virtudes c<92>vicas de nosotros los paraguayos. Con su testimonio de vida, el Papa Francisco es una persona de quien tenemos mucho que aprender y, en solo dos a<96>os de pontificado, ya nos ha dejado abundantes ense<96>anzas, sobre todo de humildad y apertura. Por sobre todo, el hecho que el mismo sea muy allegado a nuestra tierra nos conecta a<9c>n m<87>s a sus testimonios. Sus reflexiones y acciones van mucho m<87>s all<87> de lo estrictamente religioso, abarcando consideraciones sobre aspectos sociales, pol<92>ticos, medio ambientales e, inclusive, econ<97>micos. Como ejemplo, en una de sus reflexiones nos dec<92>a: <d2>La econom<92>a, como la palabra misma lo indica, deber<92>a ser el arte de alcanzar una adecuada administraci<97>n de la casa com<9c>n, que es el mundo entero<d3>. En palabras sencillas el Papa Francisco nos dice que, si bien todo crecimiento es bueno, <8e>ste deber<92>a basarse en un sano equilibrio. Es decir, no basta con crecer o acumular riquezas todos los a<96>os, sino que debemos hacerlo a un ritmo sostenible para que la sociedad no corra el riesgo de asumir costos muy elevados en el mediano y largo plazo como consecuencia de este mayor crecimiento. Uno de estos potenciales costos es la sobreexplotaci<97>n de recursos naturales, lo cual pone en peligro la vida del planeta ya que la econom<92>a mundial no puede crecer m<87>s all<87> de la capacidad de sustentaci<97>n del ecosistema. Pero adicionalmente, puede existir un elevado costo social. Justamente, el Papa Francisco recalca que <d2>los derechos humanos no solamente son violados con actos terroristas, represiones o asesinatos, sino tambi<8e>n con estructuras econ<97>micas injustas que generan grandes desigualdades<d3>. Un crecimiento que ampl<92>a las brechas sociales y genera empleos precarios no es satisfactorio. El crecimiento econ<97>mico deber<92>a ser sostenible reduciendo tanto la pobreza como la desigualdad o la brecha entre los m<87>s ricos y los m<87>s pobres. Pero una sociedad m<87>s igualitaria no es solo moralmente deseable, sino que hace sentido desde un punto de vista estrictamente econ<97>mico. Un reciente estudio del FMI resalta que la desigualdad econ<97>mica resta potencial de crecimiento, por lo que si se quiere revitalizar la actividad econ<97>mica es m<87>s <9c>til impulsar el avance de los estratos con menos ingresos de la sociedad. En los <9c>ltimos diez a<96>os, Am<8e>rica Latina (incluyendo el Paraguay) ha transformado la situaci<97>n socioecon<97>mica de la regi<97>n, incrementando su clase media hasta niveles nunca antes vistos, reduciendo la desigualdad y sacando a millones de personas de la pobreza. Si bien se ha empezado a caminar por el sendero correcto, todav<92>a resta mucho por hacer. El contexto actual de desaceleraci<97>n econ<97>mica global y condiciones externas menos favorables para nuestros productos crean nuevos desaf<92>os. Se acabaron los vientos de cola. El dise<96>o de pol<92>ticas p<9c>blicas adecuadas que promuevan el crecimiento y el bienestar de todos ser<87>n fundamentales en la nueva coyuntura. Pero este Papa <d2>revolucionario<d3>, no solo predica con sus palabras, sino tambi<8e>n con sus acciones. Uno de sus primeros cambios dentro de la curia romana, fue la creaci<97>n de la Secretar<92>a de Econom<92>a del Vaticano con el objeto de racionalizar los gastos e intensificar la vigilancia en las finanzas vaticanas. <c1>Qu<8e> ejemplo! Sin ser doctor en econom<92>a, el Papa entendi<97> muy bien que tener las finanzas p<9c>blicas en orden y cuentas fiscales sanas y transparentes, es una condici<97>n inicial ineludible para cualquier pa<92>s o Estado, incluyendo el Vaticano. Igualmente, el Papa Francisco, con su sencillo ejemplo, nos recuerda a los que desempe<96>amos cargos en la administraci<97>n p<9c>blica que estamos ah<92> para servir. Recuerdo aquel inolvidable momento luego del humo blanco y del emocionante <d2>Habemus Papa<d3>. Todos esper<87>bamos que aparezca el nuevo Sumo Pont<92>fice vestido de un intenso rojo y dorado, siguiendo la tradici<97>n romana. Sin embargo, pudimos ver salir en el balc<97>n a un sencillo hombre con una austera sotana blanca y sin estola. En ese momento nos dimos cuenta de que algo iba a cambiar. De hecho, en la celebraci<97>n realizada al inicio de su pontificado mencion<97> que <d2>Nunca olvidemos que el verdadero poder es el servicio<d3>. Es su manera de decir <d2>estoy aqu<92> para servirles<d3> y mostrar que lo importante no son los que ejercen coyunturalmente el poder, sino el pueblo. Ejercer ese poder desde el gobierno, implica una mayor responsabilidad hacia la atenci<97>n de los m<87>s d<8e>biles y necesitados. Esto lo resalto el Sumo Pont<92>fice diciendo: <d2>Es imperioso que los gobernantes y los poderes financieros levanten la mirada y ampl<92>en sus perspectivas, que procuren que haya trabajo digno, educaci<97>n y cuidado de la salud para todos los ciudadanos<d3>. Nosotros, los encargados de tomar decisiones de pol<92>tica debemos recordar su ejemplo todos los d<92>as y ser sensibles a las necesidades de la gente y no perder de vista el hecho de que, con nuestras acciones, debemos procurar un mayor bienestar social para todos, sin distinci<97>n. Otra de las ense<96>anzas del Papa Francisco, que es particularmente importante para nosotros los paraguayos, se refiere a la actitud o a esa mala costumbre de concentrarnos muchas veces en lo negativo en lugar de lo positivo. Hace unos d<92>as, nos sent<92>amos orgullosos de como nuestra querida albirroja iba sorteando paulatinamente los obst<87>culos para ubicarse en la semifinal de la Copa Am<8e>rica. Pero esa semifinal no tuvo el desenlace que todos esper<87>bamos. A medida que transcurr<92>a el partido, muchos autom<87>ticamente transformaban r<87>pidamente ese orgullo en frustraci<97>n y negativismo, desmeritando los logros que ya hab<92>an alcanzado nuestros compatriotas y que hab<92>a dejado el nombre de nuestro pa<92>s nuevamente en alto. Me hizo acordar lo que dijo una vez el Papa a un grupo de comunicadores: <d2>Claro que a veces ocurren cosas negativas, pero a menudo manipulamos los hechos y nos concentrarnos m<87>s en lo negativo que en lo positivo<d3>. Una baja autoestima influye en la capacidad de desarrollarnos como naci<97>n y de progresar socialmente. Es hora que dejemos de lado el <d2>auto-boicot<d3> (como llaman algunos) que muchas veces nos hacemos los paraguayos. La reciente estabilidad y desarrollo econ<97>mico del Paraguay dejan boquiabierto a m<87>s de uno y los n<9c>meros hablan por s<92> solos. El peri<97>dico digital USA Hispanic se hizo eco hace unos d<92>as de un comentario de un profesor universitario y analista pol<92>tico. El mismo se<96>alaba que "el Paraguay no necesita de enemigos externos si nosotros mismos nos disparamos entre nosotros. No hay una l<92>nea divisoria entre la sana cr<92>tica que todos podemos y debemos hacer a nuestros gobernantes y la actual auto destrucci<97>n que presenciamos diariamente". Se<96>oras, se<96>ores: si bien perdimos la semifinal contra Argentina, somos campeones mundiales para controlar la inflaci<97>n seg<9c>n el Foro Econ<97>mico Mundial. Adem<87>s, les comento que s<92> llegamos a la final de la Copa Am<8e>rica, ya que somos vice campeones del continente en tener la menor deuda p<9c>blica y solamente somos superados por Chile. Claro que queda mucho por hacer para ser el pa<92>s que todos queremos. Pero el cambio s<97>lo es posible mediante actitudes cr<92>ticas y exigentes, junto con acciones comprometidas y responsables de todos. Aprendamos los paraguayos a mirar al Paraguay con los mismos ojos con que lo hacen much<92>simos extranjeros. Esto incluye no solo las calificadoras de riesgo, organismos multilaterales o inversores internacionales, sino a cualquier visitante casual que queda sorprendido con los progresos que se han dado recientemente en el pa<92>s. El propio Papa Francisco tiene una elevada consideraci<97>n hacia el Paraguay y sus habitantes. En su momento, el mismo record<97> como nuestro pueblo supo sobreponerse a una guerra devastadora e injusta. Mucho de ello gracias a la mujer paraguaya, la m<87>s gloriosa de toda Am<8e>rica. No me olvido de sus palabras <d2>Desear<92>a que alg<9c>n d<92>a el Comit<8e> del Premio Nobel le otorgara el Premio Nobel <c1>a la mujer paraguaya!<d3>. Siguiendo sus ense<96>anzas, valoremos entonces los avances que hemos alcanzado como sociedad, transitemos juntos el camino del desarrollo de nuestra naci<97>n, aprendamos a realizar cr<92>ticas objetivas y constructivas. Solo as<92> ser<87> posible alcanzar el pa<92>s que todos los paraguayos queremos. La visita del Papa es un hecho hist<97>rico que perdurar<87> en la memoria de todos los paraguayos. Nuestra moneda el guaran<92>, desde su mismo nombre, representa la diversidad y la riqueza de nuestra cultura y en ella est<87> plasmada nuestra esencia como paraguayos. El Banco Central considera que el m<92>nimo aporte que podr<92>a realizar para homenajear a nuestro ilustre visitante es mediante una de las formas de expresi<97>n de nuestra sociedad: el guaran<92>, nuestra moneda nacional. As<92>, el BCP se adhiere a la gran alegr<92>a y esperanza de los paraguayos ante la visita de su Santidad y ha puesto todo su esfuerzo para la acu<96>aci<97>n de una moneda conmemorativa alusiva a la visita del Papa Francisco. Esta moneda es muy sencilla, siguiendo las ense<96>anzas de quien homenajea. En el anverso lleva impreso el grabado del rostro del Papa Francisco con una cruz y la inscripci<97>n de <d2>Francisco bendice al Paraguay<d3> en la parte superior. En la parte inferior est<87> escrito <d2>Mensajero de la alegr<92>a y de la paz<d3> en la lengua que m<87>s nos identifica, el guaran<92>. En el reverso lleva una ilustraci<97>n de nuestro escudo nacional con la inscripci<97>n de <d2>Rep<9c>blica del Paraguay<d3> en la parte superior y <d2>1 Guaran<92><d3> en la parte inferior. Justamente "Mensajero de la alegr<92>a y de la paz" es el sobrenombre que le dimos los paraguayos al Papa Francisco como agradecimiento a su visita al pa<92>s. Coincidentemente, este mensajero viene a compartir su alegr<92>a y su paz con un pa<92>s que, de acuerdo a la encuestadora Gallup, es el m<87>s feliz del mundo. La emisi<97>n de esta moneda representa la forma sencilla a trav<8e>s de la cual el Banco Central del Paraguay rinde un merecido homenaje y da la bienvenida al Papa Francisco. Muchas gracias.

Title: President of BCP highlights Paraguay as the host country of the upcoming Annual Meeting of the IDB/IIC Governors in 2017.
Subtitle: Esta maana se llev a cabo el lanzamiento de la 58 Reunin Anual de Gobernadores del BID y la 32 Reunin de la Corporacin Interamericana de Inversiones (CII) 2017, que tendr lugar en Asuncin...
text: LAUNCH OF THE IDB/IIC BOARD OF GOVERNORS 2017 . Good morning everyone, welcome to the Central Bank of Paraguay. It is a pleasure to receive you in our institution and, even more, it is truly a pride the reason that brings us together: the launch of the next Annual Meeting of Governors of the Inter-American Development Bank and the Inter-American Investment Corporation, to be held in Paraguay, after 52 years. . Many events relevant to our economy occurred that year of 1965: the IDB Annual Assembly, the inauguration of the first television channel Canal 9, the inauguration of the Friendship Bridge. . Today I would like, first of all, to recognize the valuable contribution that the relationship forged with the IDB has meant for the country, a link that dates back to its constitution in 1959, being our country a founding partner. . The IDB's support for our development has been very important, from the first loan in 1964 for the construction of the Acaray Hydroelectric Power Plant to cooperation for major institutional reforms. In the financial field specifically, it is worth mentioning its contribution to second-tier banking, to the review and implementation of the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion, as well as to policies to support microcredit, among others. . For Paraguay it will be an honor to host this event, which usually hosts more than 3,000 participants, leaders of the public and private sectors, from the 48 member countries of the multilateral organization. I believe that our country will be the right setting to discuss and exchange experiences on the thematic focus of the event: youth, innovation and competitiveness. . Why is it appropriate to talk about youth in Paraguay? Because this is a country that has 70% of its population under 35 years old. We know what it's all about. Young Paraguayans have never been passive or conformist. Since our independence, they have defended the interests of the homeland, promoting positive transformations. It was several young Paraguayans who carried out our independence process: in 1811, Pedro Juan Caballero was 25 years old, Vicente Ignacio Iturbe 25, Fernando de la Mora 26, Juan Bautista Rivarola only 22 years old! . More recently, millennials have stood out as promoters of reforms in our universities and, in a way, have become controllers of public management. They have taken very seriously the words of Pope Francis in his last visit to Paraguay: "make a mess" and they are doing it in an organized way. In this regard, government policies aimed at this segment of society become particularly important for our country (and why not for our region). The demographic bonus that we have and which is not eternaldemands the commitment of the authorities to take concrete actions in a timely manner. . In terms of innovation, Paraguay has success stories that deserve to be highlighted. The livestock sector, for example, has been investing in technology since the 70s and this has shown its results, especially in the last 10 years. The country became the sixth largest exporter of meat worldwide. Even in recent months it has begun to export live cattle, which is a recognition of the genetics and quality of Paraguayan cattle. A particular case is wheat. Despite its subtropical climate, Paraguay has managed to become an importer to net producer and exporter of wheat thanks to investment in agricultural innovation and knowledge through a project that involved the public and private sectors. . Of course, there are many challenges if we are to successfully face the so-called "fourth industrial revolution". In the new era, which will demand primarily technological skills and where innovation is key, the ability to coordinate between the public and private sectors will be fundamental. . As for the third approach, competitiveness, Paraguay has come a long way. Today, thanks to its competitiveness, the country is positioned as the world's leading exporter of organic sugar and renewable energy; fourth largest exporter of soybean oil; World's sixth largest exporter of meat, wheat and maize. But, under the new global conditions with low commodity prices and more adverse financial conditions, it will be necessary to work much more and better on policies that improve countries' productivity. Only in this way will it be possible to sustain high levels of competitiveness that translate into greater economic growth. . I am really looking forward to the debates that will take place in the Assembly on focused policies on all these issues. But more importantly, I am confident that the words of these debates will ultimately translate into action by implementing policies that boost income levels and increase the quality of life of our compatriots. . Ladies and gentlemen . Much has changed since that last Assembly in 1965. Paraguay has experienced important economic, social and political changes that have led our country to achieve highly valued macroeconomic stability in the region. This stability became a fundamental pillar to place Paraguay as one of the best performing economic in the region, with an average growth of almost 5% in the last decade. . It is worth noting that, since then, the Paraguayan population has practically quadrupled and the economy is 70 times larger. The GDP that was USD 400 million and today reaches USD 27 trillion. Likewise, the global demand for Paraguayan products has grown significantly, going from representing only 12% of GDP to 40% today. This greater openness was accompanied by a significant increase in our international reserves destined to face external shocks, which went from representing 2.7% of GDP to 22.3% of it. . This dynamism of the economy was not only driven by traditional sectors, but also by the unusual expansion of non-traditional ones. For example, the last Assembly was hosted by the emblematic and recently opened Guarani hotel with 171 rooms, so with great ingenuity a boat was used to accommodate part of the guests. Today, however, the hotel infrastructure has experienced exponential growth and, only in the area near the event venue, there is a hotel capacity of 1,367 rooms. This is just one example of the economic and urban development that our guests will be able to witness. . Important reforms were also carried out in the area of monetary, financial, fiscal and transparency management management. All this contributed to the country remaining one of the few in the region that retains a stable outlook in its sovereign debt rating, even in an international context of greater risks. We are aware that we are no strangers to this adverse scenario, even more so as a small and open economy. And recently, Luis Alberto, we had to review our growth prospects... but on the rise, while most countries did so in the opposite direction. It is these facts that make international media, such as Bloomberg, qualify us as champions of economic growth in the region. . How much the country and our economy have changed. But we must recognize that there are some things that have not changed absolutely since then. Of course, that's not necessarily a bad thing. For example, we have the same currency, which is now more than 70 years old, thanks to stable inflation, historically among the lowest rates in the region. So our foreign guests will be able to enjoy the rich Paraguayan meat, paying with the same monetary denomination used in the last Assembly. Few countries in the region can afford this luxury after 50 years. . All of the above makes it possible to appreciate today a Paraguay very different from that of 1965 but at the same time preserving its values and good policies. The country knew how to learn from its past mistakes to renew itself, capturing international attention more and more strongly. . The growth and economic development that Paraguay has achieved in recent years can be seen in numbers and indicators. A small but thriving economy, which is going in the right direction. The IDB assembly will be a propitious meeting for the more than 2,000 participants from abroad to corroborate the reality behind these numbers and discover or rediscover a young, innovative and competitive country. . Thanks a lot.

Por ejemplo, contamos con la misma moneda, que ahora tiene m<87>s de 70 a<96>os, gracias a una inflaci<97>n estable, situada hist<97>ricamente entre las tasas m<87>s bajas de la regi<97>n. As<92> que nuestros invitados extranjeros van a poder disfrutar de la rica carne paraguaya, pagando con la misma denominaci<97>n monetaria utilizada en la <9c>ltima Asamblea. Pocos pa<92>ses de la regi<97>n se pueden dar este lujo despu<8e>s de 50 a<96>os. . Todo lo mencionado, hace posible que hoy se pueda apreciar un Paraguay muy diferente al de 1965 pero que a la vez preserva sus valores y sus buenas pol<92>ticas. El pa<92>s supo aprender de sus errores del pasado para renovarse, captando la atenci<97>n internacional cada vez con m<87>s fuerza. . El crecimiento y el desarrollo econ<97>mico que ha alcanzado el Paraguay en los <9c>ltimos a<96>os se verifica en n<9c>meros e indicadores. Una peque<96>a pero pujante econom<92>a, que est<87> yendo en la direcci<97>n correcta. La asamblea del BID ser<87> un encuentro propicio para que los m<87>s de 2.000 participantes del exterior puedan corroborar la realidad detr<87>s de estos n<9c>meros y descubrir o redescubrir un pa<92>s joven, innovador y competitivo. . Title: BCP and CSJ signed an interinstitutional cooperation agreement.
Subtitle: Esta maana, en la Sala de Reuniones de la Presidencia de la Corte Suprema de Justicia (CSJ), el Banco Central del Paraguay (BCP) y la mencionada institucin judicial procedieron a rubricar un...
text: Speech President BCP  agreement Supreme Court of Justice . Good morning to everyone present. President of the Supreme Court of Justice, Dr. Alicia Pucheta de Correa, Ministers of the Supreme Court of Justice, . Rather, the signing of this Convention constitutes the culmination of the activities that we have already been carrying out with the officials of the Court, which have intensified in recent times. . These activities certify that our agreements are not simply written on paper or filed as a documentary Hispanic event, but are translated into concrete and specific actions that favor both institutions. . Training sessions have been organized at which officials of the Central Bank have instructed officials and magistrates of the court, for example: or the First International Seminar on Public Law or the Conference on the Principle of Legality and Good Administration, both held last year, where almost 100 officials and magistrates of the Judiciary were trained. . Within the new framework created through the agreement, a number of activities have been planned. Including: or on September 15 and 16, the second international seminar on Public Law will be held, with the participation of renowned administrative professors from Mercosur (such as Cassagne, Bacellar Filho, Celorrio, Delpiazzo and Duran Martinez, to name a few). or Realization of a seminar on legal interpretation and argumentation, with the outstanding Dr. Rodolfo Vigo. . With regard to the development of tools, we are advancing in the construction of an electrical platform that facilitates the settlement of the obligations of sums of money. What does this mean? In the judgments usually certain monetary obligations are ruled that require various complex calculations, so what is intended is the creation of an electric calculator  based on the parameters of the current legislation .that allows users of the justice system the possibility of settling the obligations in an easy and accurate way, accessing the exact amounts of the applicable interest rates according to the type of obligation, term and currency. It would practically be enough to enter a nero and the calculator throws the precise amounts. . This automation process will save time and resources as well as prevent the risks inherent in human intervention in calculation processes. Basically, they will no longer rely on interinstitutional memos of requesting information on fees, thus saving time, resources and trees. . In a short time we will be able to present a versi for consideration of the persons designated by the Court in order to initiate the process of tests and adjustments necessary for the effective implementation of this tool. . We urge the Supreme Court of Justice to take advantage of the Central Bank Institute that offers courses of various kinds, for example, on Monetary Policy, Supervision of the Financial System, the importance of Insurance, the National System for the Prevention and Fight against Money Laundering, etc. . The BCP Institute has trained, since 2014, more than 2600 people, with seminars even inside. For example, last week concluded a course in Ciudad del Este with more than 300 participants. Last Friday we held a training day with the Chamber of Senators, with approximately 50 participants. . It remains for us to put ourselves at your disposal to continue advancing in common strategies and plans that contribute to the training of qualified officials and that this, in turn, translates into more competent institutions; a fundamental condition for the development of our beloved Paraguay. . Thanks a lot.

text: SPEECH OF POSSESSION TO THE OFFICE OF INSURANCE SUPERINTENDENT Seor President of the Central Bank Dr. Jose Cantero Sienra. Members Directors of the Central Bank, Authorities and Partners National Authorities. Presidents and Officers of Insurance Companies; Representatives of the Paraguayan Association of Insurance Companies; Representatives of the Association of Insurance Producers; Representatives of the Association of Experts and Liquidators of Claims; To my family and friends here. Sisters and Beings It is a great honor for me to assume the position of Superintendent of Insurance, of the Central Bank of Paraguay, to which I arrive with much illusion and projects, after 25 as of uninterrupted work in this control body. I thank the Executive Power and the Authorities of the Central Bank of Paraguay, for the trust and support placed in me and professional management and I wish to reciprocate with responsibility, dedication and humility. I promise to fulfill my obligations and put all my capacity at the service of the Institution, giving my best effort and knowledge. I want to face this new challenge as an exciting challenge, with ideas, projects and achievements, with the firm conviction of having the support of my colleagues from the Superintendence of Insurance, who are excellent professionals, committed to a job well done, and total dedication, it is time to join forces, to add, to work together, to establish clear rules that result in a stable and solvent market. The strategic role of the Superintendence of Insurance is to ensure the solvency and stability of the insurance market, through its powers of supervision and regulation. Currently the system is composed of 35 insurance companies, 1152 insurance agents, 58 insurance brokers, 20 reinsurance brokers, 132 international reinsurers and 25 claims adjusters, it is an indispensable sector in the economic activity of our country, since insurance not only participates in the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) but its importance lies in the amount of assets that it protects, and for the investments they make within the financial system, in addition to the people they directly or indirectly employ. The premiums at the end of 2018 was 427 million dares and the accumulated from July 2018 to January 2019 amounts to the sum of 250 million dollars. These showed an upward trajectory in the period 2017-2018, with an expansion of 9% in nominal terms. And so far this current year to January growth was 7% Insurance plays an important role in improving people's quality of life. Likewise, it promotes the growth of the economy and society. Therefore, the evolution of a country will be greater the greater the share of insurance as a basic element of the economy. The challenge we have today as supervisors is to redouble efforts to create an environment conducive to sustainable market growth. Establishing solvency, transparency and consumer protection policies, contributing to the generation of trust, a fundamental pillar on which the insurance activity is based. In its regulatory role, the Superintendence of Insurance periodically updates the regulatory framework of the sector according to the needs and conditions of the national and international market, adopting the basic insurance principles issued by the International Association of Insurance Supervisors. In our role as educator and in compliance with the framework of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy (ENIF), the Superintendence of Insurance has been contributing to the education of the population in general, regarding the importance of the insurance market and the principles and foundations that govern it. Carrying out numerous educational activities aimed at different institutions, both bids and private in order to promote the insurance culture. The direction of the management of the Superintendence of Insurance is based on the parameters of SOLVENCY, STABILITY AND DEVELOPMENT of the insurance system This market faces important challenges and opportunities, for this I invite you to work together on the following objectives: 1. To direct the current method of supervision based on compliance to a risk-based supervision, strengthening the risk management systems and corporate governance of insurers and maximizing internal controls, through preventive inspections, with updated regulations with emphasis on the Basic Principles of Insurance (PBS), in accordance with the recommendations of the IAIS (International Association of Insurance Supervisors) and the ASSAL (Association of Insurance Supervisors) Latin American Insurance), 2. Strengthen the supervision of insurance entities and intermediaries in accordance with the Laws and Regulations on the Prevention of Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism, based on a system of Risk Management for obligated subjects. I encourage all components of the insurance sector to work together to face new challenges and achieve progressive and continuous change. I want to thank my family, my mother, my husband Manuel, my children Roque Francisco; Jose Manuel and Juan Pablo, for the unconditional support, for your love and for your understanding, you will forever be the engine of my life and my pride. I love you infinitely. Finally, I pray to God and to the Blessed Virgin Mary, who guide my life, to accompany me, and grant me wisdom to fulfill this mission. God Bless our Homeland and our Institution Thank you all very much for your presence.

Title: Liana Caballero assumed as a new member of the BCP Board of Directors.
Subtitle: Liana Caballero Krause asumi esta maana como nueva miembro del Directorio del Banco Central del Paraguay; el acto cont con la presencia del Ministro de Hacienda, Benigno Lpez, representantes del...
text: His Excellency, Mr. Benigno Lopez, Minister of Finance, Mr. President of the Central Bank of Paraguay, Mr. Jose Cantero Sienra, Members of the Board of Directors, Mr. Ernesto Velazquez Don Carlos Carvallo Don Diego Duarte National authorities present and representatives of the financial sector, Dear colleagues at the Central Bank, Dear Family, Ladies and gentlemen I feel a deep sense of responsibility when I assume today as a Full Member of the Board of the Institution in which I trained and that allowed me to grow professionally and personally: our beloved Central Bank of Paraguay. I especially thank His Excellency the President of the Republic, Mr. Mario Abdo Benitez, for having trusted me to exercise these functions of great relevance, as well as I thank the Minister of Finance, the President of the Central Bank of Paraguay, and the current members of the Board of Directors for having proposed my name for consideration by the National Congress. Likewise, I extend my recognition to the Honorable Chamber of Senators, which, within the framework of compliance with the constitutional requirements, gave its agreement to the appointment and gave me its vote of confidence. With affection and respect I remember the different authorities of the Central Bank, who, throughout my career, have assigned me tasks and functions of trust that allowed me to grow professionally. This is a day I will always remember, as this professional opportunity opens a very significant new stage in my life. Let me share a little of my personal story: back in 2005, recently graduated from the Economics career, I was looking for the opportunity to realize my professional dreams and that is how I agreed to a 9-month internship at the Central Bank. At the end of the internship, I knew that I wanted to be part of the staff of officials, so my joy was immense when in 2008 I joined as an official, becoming part of the Economic Studies team initially, and then moving through various sectors of the Institution. I emphasize and value that the authorities of the Central Bank have taken into account someone from the house, this is an encouraging message that our institution is committed to merit, academic training, effort and dedication, and that each one, when seeking Excellence and professional improvement, is put in line to be ready for the opportunities that are presented to us. Due to the importance and appreciation of human talent, and added, of course, to the seriousness of the management of monetary, credit and exchange policy in recent years, it is no coincidence that the Central Bank enjoys the prestige, credibility and confidence of Paraguayan society, the financial system and international markets, in a regional economic context that is currently not the most favorable. But lo and behold, the institutions built have been a solid foundation for Paraguay's macroeconomic results, which everyone praised. I highlight as one of our greatest institutional achievements, the adoption of the inflation targeting scheme as monetary policy, implemented since 2011. This scheme has made it possible to successfully reduce and control the inflation rate in recent years. It is a very valuable achievement, because although for us economists, inflation may seem merely a number, a macroeconomic metric, in reality it is a fundamental value for society, considering that it allows to maintain the purchasing power of the citizen, because it preserves the value of his money, and prevents it from deteriorating due to the uncontrolled increase in prices, which would ultimately impact their quality of life and the satisfaction of the basic needs of Paraguayan families. Hence, the preeminence of the role we play from the Central Bank to contribute to the development of our country. The positive results achieved by those who preceded me and the current colleagues on the Board are not merely accidental, but a virtuous process that must continue to be strengthened. And I want to reaffirm my commitment to continue contributing from this new position, in the same line that has been working. There are very difficult challenges ahead. The economic and financial context that the world supports today is complex. The economic dynamics of a country depend not only on its domestic factors, but on the global and regional ecosystem of which it is a part. In this sense, we are observing growing uncertainty in many international areas, such as: the normalization of the monetary policy of the United States and the trade war it maintains with China, the economic stagnation in the European Union, and the relatively weakened outlook of our neighbors: Argentina and Brazil. Paraguay managed to cope with the storms that have arisen. Our guarani, which holds the record of being one of the oldest and most stable currencies in the region, has been, in these turbulent recent times, the one that has suffered the least depreciation. From the Board of the Central Bank, we will continue to provide the elements and best practices to contribute to the process of financial stability and preservation of the value of the currency, with professionalism, technical criteria and innovation in the new climate we are experiencing. My vision, therefore, in this sense is optimistic, since I feel the support and institutional commitment of those who make up this great family of the Central Bank, and I am sure that the decisions adopted by the Board will necessarily be supported by the highly qualified personnel that the Bank has, which has the mission of executing such decisions on a daily basis. indispensable to achieve success. Teamwork, committed and coordinated, has been the key to the Bank's successes and the professional growth of its members. Companionship, as a feeling of joint effort, was and will continue to be fundamental to generate a work climate where everyone can feel confident and stimulated to give the best of themselves to the institution and the country. For this reason, I express my sincere gratitude to each and every one of the colleagues, for having contributed their grain of sand to my working life in the different moments and functions in which we had to interact. I am deeply proud to be part of this talented team that wears the BCP shirt and that with its silent work day by day, contributes decisively to national development in the Central Bank field. I can't help but mention and thank my family. To my mother, my husband Pedro, and my two children, Sebastian and Sofia, who are the pillars of my life. You are the impulse that moves me to give my best every day. Without a doubt, they are my most valuable asset. Finally, I ask God to accompany me, bless me and give me the necessary wisdom to contribute from this great responsibility entrusted to me. Again, thank you all very much!
