Title: Fernando Filrtiga Cantero assumed as a new member of the BCP Board of Directors.
Subtitle: Fernando Jess Filrtiga Cantero asumi esta maana como nuevo miembro del Directorio del Banco Central del Paraguay; el acto cont con la presencia del viceministro de Hacienda, Oscar...
text: Mr. oscar Orue, Undersecretary of State for Taxation; Mr. Jose Cantero, President of the Central Bank of Paraguay; Mr. Carlos Carvallo, Mr. Diego Duarte and Mr. Liana Caballero, Full Members of the Board of Directors; Authorities and special guests; Dear comrades of the Central Bank; My thanks to the Executive Branch in the persons of the President of the Republic and the Minister of Finance, to the Honorable Chamber of Senators and to my colleagues, the President and the Members of the Board of Directors, for the vote of confidence that I will dedicate to honor during the period of my appointment. The Central Bank is a treasure of Paraguay. Two factors combine to make it so: the strategic vision of the authorities that have succeeded each other over time, some of them present here and, fundamentally, the daily commitment of fellow officials, who make up the most qualified professional staff in the country. Paraguayan society monetizes this treasure through concrete results such as a stable currency, a solid financial system and an advanced payment system. It happens that the technicality inherent in the work of the bank sometimes conspires against the objective assessment of its role in society. The textbook example in this regard is inflation control. What is the impact on the ordinary citizen? The inflation targeting scheme incorporated by the bank in 2011 provided the tools to keep the value of the guarani stable over the years, a tremendous social achievement that we run the risk of underestimating. Let's look at it from another perspective. Inflation is a somewhat abstract name for the most unfair tax on economically vulnerable segments of the population: a trap with no escape that depreciates their money to the point of making it scarce to cover basic needs; Meanwhile, higher-income earners can keep their wealth in assets that continue to value, deepening inequality. At the end of the day, there is a net detriment to everyone. So, when we emphasize that the central bank has managed to keep the guarani stable, we are actually celebrating an essential element for development with equity, which may well not be seen, but definitely felt. That's a classic job of central banks around the world where ours excels. But the Central Bank of Paraguay, in addition to controlling inflation, carries out other activities of similar complexity and social importance, as regulator and supervisor of the financial, exchange and insurance systems; administrator of the deposit guarantee fund and international reserves; regulator of the payment system and financial advisor to the State. In turn, the bank produces and publishes the main statistics of the economy, produces scientific research and promotes training and culture through the Institute of the Central Bank of Paraguay, the library and the cultural area. In each of these functions, BCP stamps a mark of excellence. Lately, the bank's effectiveness as a monetary and financial regulator has been replicated in the payments infrastructure. In 2019 alone, the Paraguayan Payment System hosted operations for 51,000 million dollars equivalent to 129% of GDP. Now the SIPAP 24x7 project is being started so that it works at all times, 365 days a year, with lower costs for citizens. Contrary to what might seem logical, BCP is increasingly doing, with fewer resources, an endogenous efficiency equation. It is the first public institution to have implemented a sustained policy of cost rationalization, on its own initiative. In the period 2000-2019, the labor force was reduced by 30%. In the last 10 years, a system of competitive examinations has been applied for the admission of civil servants in which I myself have been a participant and is probably the most rigorous system of its kind in Paraguay. Wages and allowances have remained unchanged since 2016, which, in real terms, when incorporating the inflationary effect, describes a progressive year-on-year reduction. Other initiatives such as the replacement of the traditional vehicle fleet with electric and hybrid vehicles, as well as the zero paper program have been generating significant savings. These are some achievements of the great BCP family. We will continue the good work, focusing on our most important asset: the human factor. The Board of Directors of the BCP is a model collegiate government, where calm and participatory reflection is favored, within a framework of intellectual independence, consistent with the autonomy of the entity, which is the inseparable correlate of the technical character enshrined in the Constitution. Each member adds value to decisions from their area of expertise. In this sense, we understand that the legal role will be challenging in this period when the Board of Directors has to regulate and apply the latest reforms of our Charter and the Banking Law. It is time to set precedents that will shape national banking law in the coming years and to continue to safeguard that the technical decisions of the BCP are respected in the judicial sphere, on which its effectiveness depends. Likewise, we plan to devote special attention to the national fight against money laundering and terrorist financing in our areas of supervision, and to financial inclusion, another wide-ranging front where we must be sufficiently skilled to understand and take advantage of the new technologies applied to financial products, safeguarding consumer safety, as has already been done in the ecosystem of electronic payment methods. The expansion of the supervisory universe to include certain non-traditional actors, starting with credit houses, will continue to develop through clear and even-handed rules. The excitement of returning home is great, because in the past I have had the honor of being a career civil servant of the institution. Our commitment is to strengthen BCP's step on the path of excellence. In five years, I would like to look back and have the satisfaction of having contributed to the bank as an organization and as the exceptional human group that has always made Paraguay proud. That the bank is even more efficient, technical and independent, committed to the welfare of society. I will now allow myself a very personal note of thanks. To God, to my family, to my parents, who are responsible for all my virtues, the mistakes are mine. My grandparents and siblings, the loved ones and friends who are with me today, not only physically. And finally, the first thing in my heart... Ivanna and Octavio: you are my life. I take on this challenge with your blessing. Thanks a lot

Title: Mara Fernanda Carron and Humberto Colmn assumed as members of the BCP Board of Directors.
Subtitle: Este jueves; Mara Fernanda Carron y Humberto Colmn asumieron como miembros titulares del Directorio del Banco Central del Paraguay (BCP), en un acto realizado en el Saln Auditorio de la...
text: Good day Your Excellency, Dr. Oscar Lamosas, Minister of Finance. To be President of the Central Bank of Paraguay, Dr. Jose Cantero Seres Members of the Board Dr. Diego Duarte Dr. Fernando Filartiga Dr. Humberto Colman Seres Representatives of the Financial Sector. AUTHORITIES OF THE ASSOCIATION OF EXCHANGE HOUSES, INSURANCE COMPANIES And to all the special guests present this morning. I wish to begin by saying that I am very honored to receive this recognition, but at the same time with a great commitment to give my best efforts in the performance of this new function, I can not fail to thank all those who have placed their trust in me: to Pte. de la Replica, Mr. Mario Abdo Benitez, to the Minister of Finance, to Mr. Oscar Llamosas, to the Pte. of the Central Bank, Jose Cantero, who have honored me by proposing me as a candidate for this position. I am also grateful for the vote of confidence that the Chamber of Senators has given me, when it unanimously gave its constitutional agreement so that I can occupy the position of Full Member of the Board of the Central Bank of Paraguay. My professional career took place mainly in the private financial sector, where I worked more than 22 years. I started my career within a foreign-owned bank, a large school bank, especially in terms of institutional policies and international best practices. Subsequently, I had the great opportunity to be part of a financial institution mostly Paraguayan-owned, this entity allowed me to know the country, travel the interior of the country recognizing the potential of the productive sector, a great engine of our economy. I can say that I had the opportunity to know almost all the tasks of a financial institution, from the reception area of a bank where I took my first steps through almost all departments and functions, international trade, International Int to finally become a Gte. General Adjunta in the last as. This knowledge of all internal processes gives me today an opportunity to give a contribution from the management experience of a financial institution to this institution. After those 22 ace of activity in the private sector, I receive a "call", the opportunity to be part of the Board of the Development Finance Agency and contribute to the country from the plico. I confess that the proposal, at that time, meant a great challenge for me and placed me with a dilemma: stay in my comfort zone or take that leap, move from the private sector to the plico, contribute to the implementation of policies in a more direct way. Finally, I made a decision that fills me with satisfaction, that of contributing to the country from an institution as prominent as AFD, which I knew and admired for its excellence and professionalism even before being part of this, a model institution. I think it is safe to say that, at the beginning of 2020, no government, no financial institution and none of us could measure what we would have to face at that time and how valuable the role of the public sector and development banks would be, granting loans under unbeatable conditions at a time of high uncertainty, which helps counteract the negative effects of the pandemic. Thus, with the implementation of monetary, financial, regulatory and fiscal stimulus well Coordinated, allowing Paraguay to minimize its adverse impacts, protect the most vulnerable population and facilitate rapid economic recovery. At that time we redoubled our efforts to adapt to the circumstances and live up to the needs of the moment, implementing in record time a development instrument that was fundamental, strengthening the guarantee fund that was one of the indispensable instruments during the crisis, which allowed thousands of Paraguayans to access financing thanks to the commitment of the banks and private sector. Today, looking back, I can say that the success of these measures is fundamentally due to the permanent articulation with the unions, the private financial sector and the public, where I emphasize my firm conviction that a country is built with commitment and assuming all our responsibilities, and at fundamental moments prioritizing the common good before particular interests. From my experience in AFD I can say that private partnership is an important tool for the development of the country, with which we generate confidence and better opportunities. At this moment I am faced with a new call, to contribute to my country serving from the Central Bank of Paraguay and I have to leave an institution to which I have a lot of care, to assume such an important position in an entity that I admire deeply, for its technical professionalism, and for its efficiency and independence in the management of monetary policy and financial supervision. This has allowed the sustained economic growth of Paraguay, consequently, the increase of the international rating and a country image that allows the increase of investments in recent years. This fills me with pride, but at the same time represents for me a great responsibility: to preserve what has been achieved by this institution through many ace of effort and professionalism How to be:  The stability of the currency: through the implementation of the inflation targeting scheme since 2011, the downward trend in inflation has been consolidated. And this drop in inflation has allowed to maintain the purchasing power of thousands of Paraguayans, and from there improve their quality of life.  A financial system been, stable, reliable, in which we could observe the growth of depitos by 19% in 2020, that is, Paraguayans trust the financial system, this is not the result of chance, but of an efficient and independent supervision together with the commitment and effort of the financial system in the timas decades. With the exceptional measures in monetary and financial matters to face the challenges of the pandemic, we have ahead of us a period of normalization that is challenging for everyone, both from regulation and from financial institutions, for which we must apply this strategy of plico-private partnership to sustain the process of financial development.  The promotion of financial education and inclusion is essential to promote that more Paraguayans can access the formal financial system, can access credit opportunities, this translates into opportunities for education, housing, starting a business. I believe it is essential to incentivise economic and educational opportunities for the most vulnerable sectors of society given the clear evidence that this will support inclusive economic growth more broadly.  Also continue to support policies that promote gender equality, the inclusion of more women in the financial system. I celebrate the decision of BCP to include more and more women in decision-making areas, I have to replace the excellent management made by Dr. Liana Caballero, you can not build an institution, a country excluding half of the population, diversity is always constructive. ............. and the implementation of care policies and Mitigation of risks related to the environment.  I have full confidence that the BCP can take firm steps to consolidate progress in these areas, through prudent regulation of the financial system that promotes innovation and development in the country, based on macroeconomic stability and predictability. I am sure that this will be possible thanks to the excellent human and professional group that makes up the Central Bank staff. We have the best technicians in the country, a staff that has allowed BCP to be recognized for its excellence both locally and internationally. As I said at the beginning, everything is achieved as a team and by prioritizing institutional and national interests over individuals. Finally, I would like to mention those people who accompany me every day and who made it possible for me to be in this place today. I want to thank my colleagues who compared me throughout my professional career, those who supported me with their trust, with their example and enenzas, those who forced me to challenge myself and especially those who did not make the easy way for me but encouraged me to persist in adversity; to my family, starting with my dad; that he is no longer physically with us, but he leaves me the legacy of his honesty, the sense of dignity of work and the vocation of service in post of the construction of a better country. To my mother, to teach me the value of tenacity, the sense of reality and discipline; to my husband Patricio, who accompanies me and supports my professional development but above all my personal development, encouraging in good times and bad and finally my sons Patricio and Fabrizio, who accompany me unconditionally, believe in my dreams, believe in me and that although many times they do not understand are the main reason for being here today, to ratify my commitment and effort in this new function, and through BCP seek to build a better country for them, thank you! And thank you all for your attention.
